1.1: 1.1 I made a discourse. That is, I wrote: for to write is to work. Or he says this because by his deeds he deserved to be the writer of the Gospel. I made. The whole book of the Gospel is called one discourse, because it has one meaning; or the singular is put for the plural. The Gospel is good tidings, by which are announced rest after labor, a kingdom after servitude, life after death. Of all things. Of the words and deeds of Christ which he judged worthy of his office or suited to his dispensation. Theophilus. Theophilus is the same as friend of God, or lover of God: and if you are a friend of God, it is written to you. What Jesus began to do. From the baptism of John, in which Jesus was baptized, until the day on which he was taken up into heaven: for Luke wove together the discourses of that whole time, who at the end of the Gospel wrote thus: When he had blessed them, he departed from them and was carried up into heaven. To do. He establishes or instructs a good teacher, who does what he teaches.
1.2: 1.2 Commanding the apostles to preach the Gospel through the Holy Spirit, through whom the Gospel was preached, because he inspired the words and gave confidence. Or, commanding through the Holy Spirit, that is, what the Son commands, the Holy Spirit also commands. Or, he commanded on account of the Spirit, because he would not have commanded unless the Spirit were about to come. He chose. This turns to the praise of the apostles, whose acts he proposes to write. Taken up. Taken up by the Godhead, or taken up by a cloud, as a true man.
1.3: 1.3 Alive. A living and real body, not a phantasm, which the apostles also recognized as most familiar. Or alive, because he was living after death. Or alive, that is, no longer to die. Through days. Yet he did not appear to them for forty continuous days: for John says that four other days intervened after the day of the resurrection. After these he appeared again for forty: because he had been dead for forty hours, for forty days he confirms that he lives. And the forty can be understood as a type of the present age, in which Christ dwells in the Church: or because man, made up of four elements, is instructed against transgression of the Decalogue.
1.4: 1.4 Eating with them. He proclaims the signs of a true body, because he proved that he had risen not by one sense of the body, but by sight, hearing, touch, by appearing, speaking, eating together. The promise, which he promised through Joel, as is found in what follows: and although made by Christ, yet it will be fulfilled by the Father. Or it is called the Father's, because it is promised in his Word, that is, Christ.
1.5: 1.5 That John. BEDE. When the Lord said: That John baptized with water, but you, etc., down to what did not happen in the baptism of John. Baptism is given in two natures, namely bodily and spiritual: because the man who is baptized consists of two things, namely body and soul, yet there is one baptism, as there is one man. But you, etc. When Peter denied him, the apostles had not been baptized; not with water, but with the Spirit: for after the resurrection it was said: But you shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit. For they had not yet been confirmed by the resurrection of Christ and the sending of the Spirit. But as circumcision was not necessary for the righteous before it was commanded to Abraham and his posterity, so after the sacrament of the New Testament, that is baptism, was given in place of circumcision by the Lord saying: Unless a man be born again of water and the Holy Spirit John 3, etc., it is certain that no one belongs to the body of Christ unless he is baptized, except those to whom martyrdom is reckoned in place of baptism. Again, it is written when Paul was baptized: and it is not written when the other apostles were baptized: but we ought to understand that they were baptized because of that saying: Unless a man be born again, etc.
1.7: 1.7 It is not for you to know. He does not say, it will not be, but it is not: noting that they are still weak, and therefore not fit to know the secret. But when he says: It is not for you to know, he shows that he himself knows, to whom belong all things that are the Father's, but it is not expedient for them to know, but that they should live as if to be judged every day. Which the Father. The time of that kingdom, he says, is so secret that it lies open only to the knowledge of the Father, but you shall receive the power of the Holy Spirit, so that what you cannot do because of the weakness of the flesh, you may be able to do by the power of the Holy Spirit. In his own power. He said this as a true man, excusably, but there is only one power of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit: the Son also is the power of the Father.
1.8: 1.8 But you shall receive. The knowledge of the times is taken away, but the divine help they need is supplied: in the same way, when something is taken from children, something else is given so that they are not utterly saddened. Of the Holy Spirit coming upon you. When the Spirit comes upon you, he will not bring the kingdom of Israel, or the kingdom of God in Israel, as you suppose, but will furnish you the power of bearing witness about me, and the time of that kingdom is so far off that first the fame of the Gospel runs not only through Jerusalem, but through all the borders of Judea and Samaria, and even around to the ends of the world. In Jerusalem and in all Judea. The sequence of order is preserved in the names of the places: after Jerusalem comes the nearest province, Judea, to which Samaria is joined by its situation, then the communion of all the earth is added. In Jerusalem. Mystically: in the vision of peace, in the confession of the true faith: in the keeping of God's commandments: and he foretold that they would preach among those who have made themselves strangers to the land, through whom, like the spokes of a wheel from the middle of the earth where he wrought salvation, spiritual grace and saving doctrine flowed down through the whole world.
1.9: 1.9 And when he had said these things. Mark relates it differently, saying: And the Lord Jesus, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven Matt. 28. But because Luke added more significantly: When he had said these things, he was lifted up, he shows that the Lord ascended to heaven when those words which he had recalled were completed.
1.11: 1.11 Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking up to heaven? In whom the understanding ought to be more prudent, because the Galileans excelled the other Jews in wisdom. Or, Galileans are changeable, because through the instability of their mind they will forget the precepts of God.
1.12: 1.12 Then they returned, etc. The return of the apostles from the Mount of Olives to Jerusalem signifies the Church, which, ascending from the active life to the contemplative, descends again into the active way of life. For the Mount of Olives was called by the ancients the mount of three lights: namely of the lamp shining forth from the temple, and of the sun rising on the other side, and of the natural light of the oil on the mountain itself: which three agree with perfection, on account of the light of the divine Word shining from the Church, on account of the brightness of the sun of justice, on account of the radiance of a pure conscience.
1.13: 1.13 And when they had entered. In the Greek it is put thus: When they had entered the city, they went up to the upper room, where Peter was staying, etc. In the Greek the order of the names is thus: Peter and Andrew, James and John, Simon Zelotes and Judas of James. Upper room, etc. BEDE. It is a place on the upper level, signifying that, lifted from the earth, they climb to the heights of knowledge and virtue. The upper room is called the third story, a figure of charity built upon faith and hope. For charity is poured forth in our hearts by the Spirit. Peter and John. Peter is put first, because he is prince and shepherd. Peter and John are rightly put first, who ran together to the tomb, because they loved more than the rest. The first (if it is right to say so) loved more than the rest: the other Jesus loved most. The list of the apostles is given so that no false ones outside these may be received: and the places of each are set down equally, the grades of merit making distinctions. These are the twelve sons of Jacob; the twelve springs of the desert, which Israel found in Elim; the twelve loaves of proposition; the twelve stones on the garment of the high priest; the twelve signs of the zodiac; the twelve stones of the altar; the twelve stones raised from the Jordan; the twelve oxen under the bronze sea; the twelve stars in the crown of the bride; the twelve foundations; the twelve gates; the twelve months of the year; the twelve hours of the day; the twelve fruits of the tree of life. Zelotes. BEDE. Zelotes is the same who is called Canaanite in the Gospels. Cana is interpreted zeal. For he was from the village of Galilee where the Lord changed water into wine. He ruled the Church of the Jerusalemites after James his brother. With the son of perdition perishing, the number of the apostles remained incomplete; for like the moon the Church waxes and wanes: but old things pass away, and new are made.
1.14: 1.14 Mary, etc. The Virgin is distinguished from the women, although a woman is sometimes so called not for corruption but for sex. Behold, the beginning of the nascent Church is adorned with the flower of virginity. In the midst of the brethren. That is, of the sons, of whom one is the Father in heaven. Peter is said to have stood in the midst: as if condescending out of common compassion. This example is to be taken up by the shepherds of the Church. This number, one hundred and twenty, matches the age of Moses, so that as under this number, when Moses was dead, Jesus succeeded, who led the people into the promised land, so in the Church the primacy of Christ succeeded the old law, leading the true Israel to the kingdom of heaven.
1.18: 1.18 He possessed a field. Not that he possessed a field, but that the price of the field was his who sold the Lord of life. Having lost the land of the living, Judas possesses a field of blood and death, the eternal memory of his crime and his name. Yet he did not possess the field of the potter bought with the price of blood, for he straightway punished in himself the crime of betrayal, but possessed is said for caused to be possessed. Some ridiculously explain the field possessed by Judas as hell. Others think he possessed that field because he was buried in it with strangers. Bowels. The bowels, which are the seat of fraud, burst by so great a crime, could not hold themselves together. Rightly, however, the bowels are poured out through the seat of deceit, not through the place of the kiss, that is the mouth with which he kissed Jesus, though with a false surface, but through another part, in which was the poison of hidden malice.
1.19: 1.19 Of them, that is, of those dwelling in Jerusalem, because although both spoke Hebrew, yet the peculiarity of the language of the Jerusalemites differed from that of the Galileans, from whom the apostles were: which is shown in the Lord's passion, where even Peter, against his will, was betrayed by his speech as a Galilean.
1.20: 1.20 Let it be made desolate, and let there be none, etc. Until Matthias is chosen and taken in his place. Or, let Judas himself not be the one who dwells in it, but let another be taken in place of him who was judged unworthy of repentance.
1.23: 1.23 Two. Clement relates that these two who were set up for the lot of the apostolate were of the number of the seventy disciples. Who was surnamed. He lingers over the praise of Barnabas: because Matthew counts it for praise that he is chosen by lot. The praise of Barnabas is heaped up, lest he should seem to be rejected as unworthy: which was declared afterward; because he is ordained apostle of the Gentiles with Paul, reserved for that office. Justus. It is either Latin or Hebrew: and is interpreted sparing, or lifted up. And Matthias, who is interpreted given, or gift of God: to whom the gift of the apostolate was conferred by the Lord, or is interpreted cloth of God. Rightly, says Arator, he who was just is surpassed by the praise of men, for the little one.
2.1: 2.1 In the same place. That is, the upper room into which they had gone up. He who desires the Spirit, rising above the dwelling of the flesh by contemplation of the mind, treads it underfoot.
2.2: 2.2 From heaven. The Spirit is given from heaven, that God may be loved; on earth he is given, that the neighbor may be loved: for he was given twice after the resurrection to commend the two precepts of charity. A sound. The speech of tongues sounding from the mouths of the apostles can be called a sound. The Spirit. Before the passion the Spirit was given to the apostles for the grace of teaching and of healings; after the resurrection Jesus breathed on them and said: Receive the Holy Spirit; whose sins you forgive, they are forgiven them John 20, etc. This gift he had earlier given to Peter alone: but, as is believed, it was then given by anticipation, now with the others by completion it is granted to Peter also: and the power of forgiving was given to those whom he was sending to the office of preaching. Mighty. By comparison with the earlier gifts the grace of the apostles is called mighty, or the Spirit came in the likeness of a mighty wind. The whole house. The Spirit is poured out on those sitting in one house, to commend the unity of the Church, in the upper room, as the third law begins. At the giving of the law the people stood far off for fear; here, at the coming of the Spirit, they were gathered into one out of love. Sitting. That what had been said to them might be fulfilled: Sit here in the city. Sitting is a sign of humility and steadfastness: a seat is prepared for the Holy Spirit in these, who rests upon the humble. GREGORY. The Spirit appeared in fire, but by himself, etc., down to hearts were taught both by voice and by sound.
2.3: 2.3 Parted. The dispersion of tongues happened at the tower, but what pride scattered, humility gathers again: in pride is dispersion, in humility concord comes about. Behold, the saying of the Lord is fulfilled, who said: I will not leave you orphans, but I will send the Spirit, the Paraclete John 14, who, as their advocate, spoke for them in all tongues. He who came for the Word brought tongues, for the tongue has kinship with the word, so that they cannot be separated from each other. So the Word of the Father, that is the Son, and the Holy Spirit are inseparable, indeed of one nature. As of fire. The Spirit likewise came in fire: because the Spirit purges, enlightens, kindles, burns sinners. For fire has four natures: it burns, purges, warms, illuminates. Similarly the Spirit burns away sins, purges hearts, shakes off torpor, lights up ignorance. Fire is incorporeal and invisible in its own nature; but when it takes up some body it is seen, appearing of different colors, because of the materials in which it burns. So the Spirit could not be seen except through the creatures in which he works.
2.4: 2.4 And they began. Behold the sign of fullness: a full vessel bursts forth. Fire in the bosom cannot be hidden. With various tongues. Because they spoke in all tongues, or, speaking in their own, that is the Hebrew tongue, they were so understood by all as if they were speaking in the language of each, according to the saying of the Prophet: In other tongues, and by other lips, I will speak to this people, etc.
2.5: 2.5 From every nation, etc. RABANUS. As if to say: Wherever they were born. The captivity, which took place under Antiochus not many times before, caused Jews to be born among all nations.
2.6: 2.6 Confounded. This confusion is set against the confusion of tongues, from which Babel got its name. So the humility of the apostles answers the pride of men. Each one. The tongues are all said to be seventy-two: whence the disciples of the second rank were chosen under this number, so that the number of the preachers might agree with the number of the tongues.
2.8: 2.8 We have heard. In this it was signified that the one Church would speak in the tongues of all nations. BEDE. The question is asked whether those who were speaking, etc., down to the miracle seemed to belong more to the hearers than to the speakers.
2.9: 2.9 Cappadocia, etc. These five provinces which are put after Judea speak Greek indeed: but from the custom of their country there is a diversity in sound. Whence the grace in the apostles was wonderful, which taught them not only the diversity, but also made in their speech the distance between the peculiarities in each of the languages, according to the number of the provinces.
2.10: 2.10 Strangers of Rome. In the Greek, sojourning Romans, that is, Jews who led a life of sojourning at Rome.
2.14: 2.14 Men of Judea. That is, there are two causes of prudence, namely that they are Jews, and that they dwell in Jerusalem, for which sobriety is fitting.
2.17: 2.17 I will pour out. By this word he shows the generosity of the gift, because the Spirit was to be given not, as formerly, only to prophets and priests, but to persons of both sexes everywhere without distinction. Of my Spirit. He has regard to the diverse gifts when he says this, but not to any lessening of the substance. Upon all flesh. Who is meant by all flesh he explains next in what follows: And your sons shall prophesy, etc. RABANUS. Upon all flesh, male and female, or circumcised and Gentile, according to the saying: There is neither male nor female, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian nor Scythian, slave nor free Gal. 3. And they shall prophesy. The law and the prophets until John: from then the kingdom is preached. But it is one thing to prophesy of Christ, another to foretell and teach things to come.
2.19: 2.19 And I will give. Mystically, wonders in heaven are labors in the Church. Signs, on the earth. Vengeances, upon earthly men. Blood, in martyrdom. Fire, of the Gospel or of the Holy Spirit. Vapor of smoke, the compunction of the soul or heart. Wonders in heaven. For when Christ was born, a new star appeared; when he ascended the cross, the sun was darkened and the sky was covered with darkness. Blood. Not only of the wound, but also of sweat, when in prayer his sweat became like drops of blood, which is counted among the signs of the Godhead, because it is not found in human nature. Therefore it signifies that the whole world was to be washed with the blood of Christ, so that as the tabernacle had been consecrated with the blood of victims, so the faithful people might be dedicated with his blood: and that not only in Jerusalem would there be a place of prayer, but in every place of his dominion the elect might lift up hands to the Lord in prayers. Vapor of smoke. Namely the vapor of compunction and of tears. For as smoke comes from fire, so compunction comes from the ardor of the Holy Spirit. The sun shall be turned, etc. This is believed to have been done partly in the passion of Christ and partly to come before the day of judgment. For then the sun was darkened, but the moon turned to blood could not appear to men: because then (as at the Passover) being fifteen days old, it had been hidden from human sight by the interposition of the earth during the day.
2.23: 2.23 By the determinate counsel. RABANUS. In this alone were the Jews notable, that they did not do it with an obedient mind. And the foreknowledge of God, etc. THE SAME. In the Greek it is thus: Receiving him thus delivered by foreknowledge. For he was delivered by the governor into their power, that they might choose either him or the robber, but life being granted to the robber, they slew Jesus by the hands of the soldiers.
2.24: 2.24 Raised up. Not by the usual, common resurrection with the rest, which is deferred to the end, but which would be celebrated on the third day, that the assertion of this resurrection might be a testimony of the Deity. RABANUS. He raised up, according to the humanity, which the Jews most hated. Having loosed the sorrows. The sense of this sentence seems to be that, the Lord descending to hell, the sorrows of the pains were loosed, because they could not touch him, but according to the Greek where it is written: Loosing through him the sorrows of death, in that it was impossible that he be held by it, it is clear that by his descent the saints were freed from the places of hell; who though in the bosom of Abraham, that is in the consolation of rest, were yet not wholly loosed from the sorrow of death or of hell, because they had not merited to enter the joys of heaven, until that of the Prophet was fulfilled: By the blood of your testament you have brought forth your prisoners out of the pit, in which there is no water, Zechariah 5. For they were bound before they were led out.
2.25: 2.25 I foresaw the Lord. The voice of Christ after the resurrection exulting at the right hand. The left is the present life; the right, eternal. That I be not moved. After the resurrection all things will be immovable. And my tongue was glad. Because rest was given after labor: for he labored in hope of eternal life. You will not leave. I shall not again be moved by the corruption of a repeated cross and death. You have made known to me. I know that I shall live always. You shall fill me with joy, that is, I shall not die again. For he is at my right hand. The cause why he is not moved is that the Lord helps at the right hand, the left not prevailing. For if he is not at the right hand, the devil occupies that part, as is said of Judas: And let the devil stand at his right hand, Psalm 108.
2.26: 2.26 And was glad. In the passion he said: My soul is sorrowful even unto death, Matthew 26: and he began to fear and be weary: to show himself true man in soul and body, and truly passible. Afterwards, however, his soul and tongue were glad, because by his passion the human race was to be saved.
2.27: 2.27 In hell. It is established that the soul was not left in hell, which, those being taken away for whom it had descended, soon returned to the heights, nor was the flesh corrupted, but glorified by swift resurrection.
2.28: 2.28 You have made known to me. Not only is this understood of him who, having once received the fullness of divine power and wisdom, destroyed death by himself, rising to life; but also of the just who, having found through him the way of truth, will return to life and be glad beholding his face: because he was seen above all and is perfect blessedness.
2.33: 2.33 Having received the promise of the Holy Spirit. Christ received it as true man, and as God pours out the Spirit, as Joel says: I will pour out, etc. Likewise the apostles receive from him the promise of the Spirit who is said in the Gospel to be sent by the Father. He has poured this out, etc. He who before said that Jesus was raised by God, now raising higher the faith of the hearers, assigns this man to be the Lord, whom he confirms to have poured out the Spirit: for this is the sign. And beautifully he used the word of outpouring: which he recalled above that the prophet Joel had set down, so that from this it may also be established that he is the Lord Jesus, who before the assumption of flesh used to speak in the prophets, who gives signs and wonders in heaven and on earth, who saves all who call upon him. And the rest which the prophet describes, as true God, he fulfills.
2.34: 2.34 Sit at my right hand. RABANUS. Peter plainly shows from this psalm that the kingdom of Christ is not earthly, but heavenly, etc., down to in the other, the same is Lord.
2.36: 2.36 Lord, him. Setting down the name of majesty and power, he shows him to be the one to whom every creature ought to be subject. Christ is the name of royal or pontifical dignity. In the law kings and priests were anointed, in figure of him. And Christ. He is truly Christ, anointed with all the fullness of the Holy Spirit, who gave of the same Spirit potentially to whom he would. Jesus whom, etc. Jesus is Lord and Christ, one person existing in two natures, because in the Godhead eternally born of the Father, in the humanity temporally made, he was incarnated in the womb of the Virgin by the working of the Holy Spirit.
2.37: 2.37 They were pricked. The prophecy of Joel is fulfilled, because after the fire of the Holy Spirit follows the vapor of compunction. Smoke is wont to draw tears, those who had mocked begin to weep, they beat the breast, give prayer to God as a sacrifice, that they may be able to taste that blood, to be saved through him, whom they had before called down upon themselves and upon their children.
2.38: 2.38 In the name. In honor, or in this form, because in one of the three the faith is contained.
2.39: 2.39 And to all. This looks back to that testimony of prophecy which he set last, namely Whoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved: which pertains specially to the calling of the Gentiles; who, made far from the children of Israel, were to be saved by invocation of the name of the Lord.
2.40: 2.40 He testified, etc., that is testimony and exhortation. Save yourselves. This is the quality of the testimony and exhortation, but Luke summed up very many words of Peter in a brief sentence. From this generation. There are two generations, one of the good, another of the wicked.
3.2: 3.2 The gate of the temple, etc. This gate was built by Jotham son of Uzziah, king of Judah, very lofty. For all the gates of the temple were on the ground, except the Beautiful which hung: which is called by the Hebrews the Gate of Jotham. BEDE. The Beautiful gate of the temple is the Lord, through whom, etc., down to the keys of heaven were given.
3.6: 3.6 Silver, etc. Peter was mindful of that precept: Do not possess gold and silver. The money also which was laid at the feet of the apostles they did not hoard for themselves, but kept for the uses of the poor, who had left their patrimonies.
3.8: 3.8 And leaping up he stood, etc. The order of perfection: first he rises who had lain down, then takes up the way of virtues, and so enters the gate of the kingdom with the apostles.
3.10: 3.10 With wonder and amazement. That is, with fear and ecstasy of mind. It is also called ecstasy when the mind is not alienated by fear, but is taken up by the inspiration of revelation. He ran, etc. BEDE. Israel being saved through the apostles, the whole world ran, etc., down to alone throughout the world holds a peaceful empire.
3.13: 3.13 The God of Abraham, etc. RABANUS. Three are named with no impious one intervening, either because of the primacy of righteousness, or, etc., down to which is also observed likewise in spiritual generation.
3.15: 3.15 You killed, by will and word, and this against the law, which says: He that kills a man willingly shall himself be put to death.
3.16: 3.16 Perfect soundness. In the two things that were foretold.
3.17: 3.17 Through ignorance. Two things cooperated: your ignorance, and the foreknowledge of God.
3.18: 3.18 By the mouth of all, etc. Therefore it was necessary to be fulfilled, because not one but all had prophesied.
3.19: 3.19 That your sins may be blotted out. Then sins will be fully blotted out, when by the power of the resurrection the last death will be destroyed.
3.20: 3.20 That when the times shall come, etc. This is said in continuation of what went before, namely, that when the times of refreshment shall come from the presence of the Lord, then your sins may be blotted out.
3.21: 3.21 Whom it behooves, etc. That is, the Church by faith, or in heaven to sit at the right hand of the Father.
3.22: 3.22 Moses indeed. He sets examples, not of all who have spoken, or what, but of some only. A prophet, etc. The Son of God took flesh from the people of Israel, appearing in the likeness of Moses, that as he led carnal Israel, instructed and purified by ceremonies and sacred laws, into the land of promise, so also Jesus by the grace of the Gospel led spiritual Israel to heaven. And as the despisers of the law of Moses were cast out from the land of promise by enemies, so those who despise the doctrine of the Gospel shall be driven from the company of the saints by the avengers of the spirit. Of your brethren. RABANUS. God raised up Joshua of Ephraim, Jesus of Judah.
3.23: 3.23 He shall be destroyed from among the people. That is, from the lot of the saints, and made an exile. Or, he shall be cast out beyond the borders of blessedness. RABANUS. Those resisting Joshua were cast out from the carnal people; but those resisting Christ are cut off from the spiritual. Death follows each disobedience, whether carnal or spiritual. From Samuel and afterwards. Under Samuel the times of kings began in Judea.
3.25: 3.25 Of the covenant. BEDE. From that covenant which to Moses, etc., down to in your seed shall all the nations be blessed. The fathers. He put the plural fathers, and not the singular father, because it was promised not to Abraham alone but to Isaac and Jacob. In your seed, etc. BEDE. The seed of Abraham is Christ - in whose faith blessing is promised to all families, to the Jews namely and the Gentiles. All the families. Not that all, but because none is blessed except in him, as also that: He enlightens every man coming into this world, John 1. Shall be blessed. Cursed in Adam's sin, they are blessed in Christ, in whom those also who preceded the incarnation are blessed: because the same God-man opened the door of heaven, and at the end will say to all the elect: Come, blessed of the Father, Matthew 25, etc.
4.1: 4.1 The priests and the magistrates, etc. These seemed to be the teachers and judges of the people. The Sadducees. These denied the resurrection: and therefore they were grieved at the doctrine of the apostles, who announced the resurrection.
4.2: 4.2 Grieved, that the multitude flocked together to hear the apostles. The resurrection. This is above all against the Sadducees: but both were grieved that Jesus, whom as man they had killed, the apostles affirmed to be glorified by God the Father.
4.4: 4.4 And the number, etc. If in the five thousand men whom the Lord fed in the wilderness the people of the law freed by Christ is understood, here too the five thousand instructed by the apostles can signify the people of the Gentiles: about to follow spiritually the mysteries of the same law. And well indeed are they endowed with the heavenly gift in the evening, because when the fullness of time came, God sent his Son on earth, etc.
4.11: 4.11 This is the stone. RABANUS. Here, answering what was asked, he preaches about Christ, and especially from David, whom, as their patriarch, they would believe before others. Rejected. AUGUSTINE. Of the rejected stone there is no history.
4.13: 4.13 Without letters, etc. Not that they knew no letters at all, but that they had no skill in the grammatical art, this was said. Unlearned. They were called unlearned because they had not exercised their own genius through teaching: in Greek, Latin, the propriety. BEDE. The unlettered are sent to preach, lest the faith of believers be thought to come not by the power of God but by eloquence: according to that: Not in wisdom of word, lest the cross of Christ be made void, 1 Corinthians 1.
4.19: 4.19 But Peter, etc. RABANUS. You who are judges, do your office, not by uttering perverse speech, but by judging justly. Behold the full grain is found in the ear: which before, like grass, was bent.
4.20: 4.20 For we cannot. That is, we will not, or it has been turned into nature (as with the confirmed angels) not to sin.
4.21: 4.21 They glorified. In the Greek: All glorified in that which was done: and not that which had happened. Deeds or words are glorified when, fame spreading, they are carried to the knowledge of very many. God is glorified in the deeds of men, which is proper to Christian piety and humility, he himself saying: Let them see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven, Matthew 5.
4.22: 4.22 For the man was above forty years old, etc. Whence the greater glory or grace of the power appeared, and therefore he speaks not of the man's age but of the time of the infirmity.
4.24: 4.24 With one accord, etc. Without sound. Or by the perfection of unanimity, according to that: If two or three agree in my name, concerning any thing whatsoever they shall ask, it shall be done to them.
4.25: 4.25 Why did the Gentiles rage. The roar is the voice of a lion. Hence Jeremiah: My inheritance is become to me as a lion in the wood: it has uttered its voice against me, Jeremiah 12. They imagined vain things. About Christ to come, or that he might be held in death.
4.26: 4.26 They assembled. Herod and Pilate were made friends.
4.27: 4.27 You anointed. They expound the name of Christ. Christ, from chrism, that is unction, according to that: God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows, Psalm 44.
4.29: 4.29 With all confidence. They ask this of God, that with all confidence they may speak the word of God.
4.30: 4.30 By the name. In the Greek: By the name of your child Jesus, which more suits the prayers of the apostles, who were eager that the man crucified by the Jews, with miracles shining, through the name of him who was taken up into heaven, the very Son of God himself might become known.
4.31: 4.31 The place was moved. Great is the power of the prayer of the faithful, and this was done to rouse their minds.
4.32: 4.32 They had one heart. Those who had left the world, not glorying in nobility of race, did not set themselves above others, but, as born from the womb of one and the same mother Church, rejoiced in the same love of brotherhood. Neither did any of them. The virtues which the just possess they judge not to be their own, but of those for whose benefit they dispense them. Common. In Greek, whence cenobites, that is those living in common. Cenobia, their dwellings.
4.33: 4.33 The apostles rendered. He distinguishes the order of teachers and hearers. For the multitude of believers, temporal things being despised, were joined to one another by the bond of charity. The apostles, however, shining in power, laid open the mysteries of Christ.
4.36: 4.36 Joseph. RABANUS. Barnabas is interpreted son of consolation, increased, by growth and progress of spiritual good. Which is interpreted. Wherever Scripture sets the names of things or persons with an interpretation, it signifies that a more sacred sense is in them. Deservedly is he called son of consolation, who, despising present things, consoles himself by the hope of the future. For the Holy Spirit also is called Paraclete because in the world he gives, by his infusion, paraclesis, that is consolation, to those having tribulation, as Peter also, because of the grace of the Spirit, was called Bar-jona, that is son of a dove. Son of consolation. RABANUS. Either on account of the alms with which he consoled the poor, or for the consolation of the reward which he deserved to receive from God, or because he was held worthy to console the apostles on behalf of Judas.
5.3: 5.3 Tempted. RABANUS. He puts the past tense tempted, because the temptation was complete. Temptation is carried out in three ways, by suasion, delight, consent: all of which was fulfilled in Ananias. And to defraud. THE SAME. In this the lie seems to have been, that he had vowed the whole. It is better, however, not to vow than after the vow not to pay to the Holy Spirit.
5.4: 5.4 But God. Above he had said: The Holy Spirit: it is clear therefore that the Holy Spirit is God.
5.5: 5.5 He fell down. RABANUS. The beginnings of laws are always commended by punishments. The two sons of Aaron offering fire are consumed: Uzzah supporting the ark died. He fell, that the other transgressors might be terrified by his example. And great fear came, etc. BEDE. Anticipation: since few had heard of the death of the man alone before his wife went out, although of the few it could be said that they feared.
5.7: 5.7 Of hours, etc. RABANUS. A little time for repentance is given to the wife, whose fault is more venial than the husband's, inasmuch as she consented to the head.
5.8: 5.8 Tell me, etc. THE SAME. By asking, he declares the wife's guilt from her own confession, which the husband had shown his in deed.
5.9: 5.9 Why, etc. Said by way of rebuke? or it is to be distinguished thus: why? as: What is this: then he answers himself and says: Is it indeed agreed between you to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? To tempt, etc. RABANUS. The tempting of the Spirit was in this, that they tested how great his knowledge is. They buried. THE SAME. From this many take example that wives be buried beside their husbands. Others think it unworthy to take examples from transgressors, to whom common fellowship had made equal merit in crime and death and burial.
5.11: 5.11 And great fear. First Ananias and Sapphira died quickly in the sight of the Church, that the apostolic authority, how great it was, might be shown: and how great a sin it was to draw back from the Church what had been offered, and that the rest might be chastened by this example.
5.12: 5.12 Of the apostles. It is said in the plural, of the apostles, because it was not by the hand of Peter alone; for though out of honor to him the others are passed over in silence, yet their deeds are not passed over.
5.13: 5.13 Of the rest, etc. By the example of Ananias and his wife: for the punishment of the two who had joined themselves to them fraudulently gave an example to the rest.
5.14: 5.14 Increased, etc. RABANUS. So great was the multitude of believers that, the strength of faith growing, the shadow alone was enough. Or: So many were then the sick brought by believers that all could not be touched.
5.17: 5.17 Heresy. RABANUS. Heresy is interpreted a cutting off, because the heretic, despising the sayings of others, chooses what he thinks to be followed. Of the Sadducees, filled, etc. Sadducees are interpreted the just, named from Zadok the priest, either from their race or from their morals; but justifying themselves they claimed for themselves what they were not: denying the resurrection of bodies, they said souls perish with the flesh: they believed neither angel nor any spirit to be, rejected all the Scriptures except the books of Moses: and therefore they especially agreed with the princes in the persecution of the apostles, who by power and signs gave testimony to the resurrection of Christ.
5.20: 5.20 Of this life. RABANUS. Of the Christian, or the eternal. This is not added, however, because the sect of the Christians was famous, for which they had been delivered to prison.
5.23: 5.23 The prison indeed, etc. The mad Jews who, stirred by envy, say that the apostles stole the body of Jesus from the tomb, by whose theft they would say the apostles were taken out of the closed prison.
5.24: 5.24 The magistrate. According to the Greek, magistrate is to be read in the singular, as also in the following where it says: Then the magistrate went with the officers. They were in doubt. Even so they do not believe: for inner malice hardens the faithless heart even against manifest signs.
5.28: 5.28 Commanding, etc. In the Greek: Did we not strictly command you? For thus to speak is more fitting to one asking. You have filled Jerusalem. The chief of cities, in which we also dwell. In this they unknowingly praise the apostles, who, not frightened by threats, do not cease to preach. Upon us the blood. RABANUS. It is clear that it was said by antiphrasis: His blood be upon us. The rash question of the high priest is refuted by a prudent answer. THE SAME. They ask, for there is wont to be doubt in words when a firm opinion is held in the heart.
5.30: 5.30 The God of our fathers. RABANUS. Not new, nor lately found by us: he says this that their disobedience may be inexcusable.
5.32: 5.32 The Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit has strengthened us, that even though you resist we may firmly preach the great works of God; speaking in us he forms the words which you hear. To all. RABANUS. Not to us alone, but to all who obey, even to you, if you are willing to receive. In this he provokes to repentance.
5.34: 5.34 Gamaliel. He was a disciple of the apostles, as is thought, remaining among the Jews by the counsel of the Apostles, to destroy the worst counsels and to mitigate their fury.
5.36: 5.36 Theudas. BEDE. Theudas persuaded many, taking their goods out of the city, to besiege the banks of the Jordan, and since he was a magician he called himself a prophet, and promised that the river would be divided and give them passage. A troop of horse coming upon him by order of the procurator Fadus, many being killed or taken, carried his head back to Jerusalem.
5.37: 5.37 Judas of Galilee, etc. Of this Josephus says that he compelled the people not to lose liberty by paying tribute to the Romans: setting forth from the law that God alone is to be served, and that those who paid tithes ought not to pay tribute. This heresy grew so much that the Pharisees and a great part of the people asked Christ whether it was lawful to pay tribute to Caesar.
5.40: 5.40 Beaten, etc. RABANUS. Behold the strength of faith is clear, which could be restrained neither by words nor by scourges. They were first forbidden by speech, now beaten with scourges.
5.41: 5.41 That they were counted worthy. They did not think themselves to labor, but to receive the greatest gift: because Blessed are they that suffer persecution for God, Matthew 6.
5.42: 5.42 And every day, etc. Often such chapters are interposed, gathering many things briefly, so that an end as it were is set to the past discourse, and a foundation to the following.
6.1: 6.1 Of the Greeks. RABANUS. Either of Gentile strangers living in the city: or, etc., down to were burdened in the daily ministry. Were neglected. THE SAME. From want they were the more burdened.
6.2: 6.2 It is not reason, etc. The Apostles show that bishops and teachers of the Church ought not to be entangled in bodily affairs.
6.3: 6.3 Look out, etc. BEDE. From this the apostles then decreed, etc., down to not without the mystery of the number seven.
6.4: 6.4 But we, etc. Of themselves they do not ask, but judge.
6.5: 6.5 And they chose, etc. RABANUS. This order is to be kept in ordinations: let the people choose, the bishop ordain. Stephen. He is put first, and alone is praised, that in one all may be praised, or that the honor of martyrdom may be first conferred.
6.6: 6.6 And praying. The common dispensation required that ministers be chosen, who when found worthy, the providence of saving counsel growing by degrees, it pleased that these same be ordained ministers of the holy altar and of the Lord's blood, as of the refection and common table. Which is proved from this, that it is said: Praying, they laid hands upon them: this is proper to those who are promoted to the office of the most holy altar. After this example prayers are made in ordinations, though the prayer of the apostles is not written.
6.7: 6.7 And the word, etc. RABANUS. It seems a kind of recapitulation, because he had said: Every day they ceased not teaching, etc., and returns to this very thing, saying: And the word of the Lord increased. THE SAME. Often in this book, and in the Gospel too, such chapters are interposed, etc., down to because the zeal had been stirred up when the people first grew.
6.8: 6.8 Stephen, in Greek; in Latin, crown: who in name forestalled what he was to prescribe in fact: because after the cross of Christ he was the first crowned with martyrdom loftily, who was stoned humbly. In Hebrew, Stephen is interpreted our rule, who suffering first became a pattern to the following martyrs of dying for Christ.
6.13: 6.13 This man. Out of contempt they do not call him by his own name, but call him man, as a carnal and base one.
7.2: 7.2 Men, brethren and fathers. Because Stephen was accused of having blasphemed against Moses and God, at the beginning of his speech he meets their calumny, saying that the God who spoke to the fathers and prophets is the God of majesty and glory. He also praises Moses: but proves them rebels and always disobedient. But he used the art of speaking toward the rebels, beginning as though fearing them: thus, Men, brethren and fathers: gentle and mild speech wins the hearer, that it may commend the speaker. He began softly, that he might be long heard, and he who refused to speak against God and the law preaches the true God at the beginning of his address. He also expounded the law so as to be the preacher of him whose destroyer he was accused of being: in the progress of his speech also, rebuking their errors, he showed vigor of soul, and that he was free from fear of the enemy. The God of glory, etc. Mindful of that precept: Love your enemies, Luke 6, etc., he announced salvation to his persecutors. In Mesopotamia. Mesopotamia is set at the head of Syria to the north. RABANUS. Mesopotamia and Haran are in Chaldea, from Mesopotamia he moved to Haran.
7.3: 7.3 And he said, etc. In Genesis it seems to be contained that after the death of his father the Lord spoke to Abraham, who died in Haran, where his son dwelt with him. But before he dwelt in the city, when he was in Mesopotamia, it was said to him: Go out of your country, etc. The land and kindred of Abraham he calls the fatherland and race of the Chaldeans, from which he had already gone out, now dwelling in Mesopotamia; but he was still held by hope and desire of returning, and therefore he hears: Go out of your land and from your kindred; not to draw out the body (which he had already done), but to pluck out the love of the heart. RABANUS. Stephen passed over the third, that is, and from your father's house: which was done on account of the great skill or lack of skill of the people.
7.4: 7.4 Then he went out, etc. RABANUS. From Ur of the Chaldees Abraham went out. Ur, etc., down to the father being dead it was said to him: Go out of your land, etc. His father, etc. THE SAME. He returns to the origin of the race of Israel, and the beginning of divine friendship, that he may omit nothing in which he might seem to blaspheme. You dwell. He said you, not we, because the apostles had already in a way left the land, and Stephen, who was now as it were placed in death.
7.6: 7.6 That his seed, etc. BEDE. It is not to be understood as though to be ill-treated, etc., down to whether in the land of Canaan, or in Egypt. Four hundred years. RABANUS. It is to be joined thus: Sojourner, etc., down to up to the division of the land of promise was completed.
7.7: 7.7 I will judge. THE SAME. Judgment sometimes signifies discernment, as there: Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause, Psalm 42. Sometimes punishment, as: Judge them, O God, Psalm 5.
7.8: 7.8 The covenant of circumcision. THE SAME. The covenant or sign was made therefore that the people of Israel, etc., down to it is signified that boasting of glory in spiritual circumcision is to be avoided. On the eighth day. RABANUS. In eight days the mystery of our circumcision is shown, who through the eighth of the New Testament (which is contained in the resurrection of the Lord and the eight beatitudes) are circumcised from vices on the eighth day.
7.9: 7.9 Sold into Egypt. Narrating briefly he passes to the end, for he was not sold first to the Egyptians, but to Ishmaelite merchants and Midianites, and they sold him into Egypt to Potiphar the priest.
7.14: 7.14 In souls. This is said according to the edition of the Septuagint interpreters. In the Hebrew only seventy are found. RABANUS. If Jacob and Joseph with two sons are not counted, etc., down to than to make his speech suspect for the sake of the Hebrew truth.
7.15: 7.15 And he went down. According to the situation of the places the going was a descent from the land of promise into Egypt, and because slavery had succeeded to liberty, Jacob with his offspring is said to have gone down into Egypt.
7.16: 7.16 They were carried over. RABANUS. By synecdoche they are said to be carried over for the sake of Joseph, to whom Jacob, etc., down to Carry my bones from hence with you, Genesis 50. BEDE. Of Joseph alone Scripture testifies that his bones, etc., down to the twelve patriarchs were not buried in Arba, but in Shechem. And were laid. RABANUS. Genesis teaches that Abraham from Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite, etc., down to they would not serve Moses, nor the Lord. In the sepulchre, etc. This is of Jacob alone, whose body his sons, taking it out of Egypt, buried in the double cave, where Abraham was buried with Sarah, and Isaac with Rebecca: and there Leah was laid: hence that city is called Hebron, that is marriage, because the fathers were buried there with their wives. He confuses two histories, and entangles one with the other. For Abraham did not buy from the sons of Hamor the sons of Shechem, but Jacob bought Shechem from them; so it is to be joined thus: They were carried over into Shechem by the sons of Hamor the son of Shechem: as if it were said, into that Shechem which Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor the son of Shechem. In Genesis Shechem is read to have been the son of Hamor, whence some think there were two Shechems, of whom one is called by Luke the father of Hamor, the other by Genesis the son. Some join the beginning and end of the sentence, saying, by the sons of Shechem, and afterwards add, of Hamor, that this place may agree with Genesis.
7.18: 7.18 Another king. This king is the devil, who loves the effeminate and hates the males.
7.19: 7.19 Our race, etc. He says our fathers, and our race, lest he seem to blaspheme the fathers.
7.20: 7.20 Acceptable to God, etc. Blessed Stephen shows that Moses did not blaspheme.
7.22: 7.22 Moses. RABANUS. Moses is the same as aquatic, because he was drawn from the water, or linen-like, because he was found in a basket smeared with pitch. Moses is a type of the Savior, who, having struck the devil, freed his own race.
7.24: 7.24 He avenged him, etc. He shows that he who did the wrong was not of his own race.
7.26: 7.26 He appeared to them. RABANUS. So Christ after the ascension appeared through the apostles to the quarreling Jews and unbelievers who resisted the apostles.
7.27: 7.27 Who made you, etc. As if Moses might answer: No one, but: God alone. There is no power but from God. Hence such an answer was received from Christ by one: O man, who made me judge or divider over you? Luke 12. Who made you, etc. In their contention he proves that they were already then contrary to the law and to Moses.
7.28: 7.28 Will you not, etc. Some think that he who was defended brought forth the matter out of anger.
7.29: 7.29 He fled. Moses was in Midian, that is, Christ among the Gentiles.
7.30: 7.30 In a flame of fire, etc. The fire in the bush is the Holy Spirit, the sins of the people like thorns, because the ardor of the Holy Spirit did not consume the sins of that people who set the dense thorns of wickedness against the benefits of God. RABANUS. The form of fire (which is not imitable) was therefore shown to them, lest any, etc., down to how ready for a man to take off his shoe.
7.32: 7.32 I am. I am is the proper word of God, according to that: I am who am, etc.: He who is, has sent me to you. Serpents are not to be feared where God present speaks.
7.33: 7.33 Loose your shoe. This admonishes us that, standing in the Church (which is holy ground), we renounce dead works.
7.34: 7.34 Seeing, etc. RABANUS. God was wholly seen, wholly heard, he sees all things, hears all things, but is said to see and hear when he has mercy. I have seen the affliction. THE SAME. I who, though I permit anyone to be tempted, yet it is not to be thought that I do not know.
7.35: 7.35 Whom they denied. Synecdoche. Many are said to have denied when one had said it, or perhaps because several consented to the one who denied. A prince. It is great praise that he is called prince and redeemer and leader out of the people.
7.37: 7.37 This is Moses. He turns back upon them the fault which they, disobedient and unbelieving, laid upon Moses.
7.38: 7.38 The words of life. RABANUS. That is, the two tables with the Decalogue, and the other commandments, of which it is said: He that does them shall live in them.
7.40: 7.40 To Aaron. THE SAME. As to a prince. They speak as ignorant of the Divinity. For the true God is not made, but made all things, nor is he a creature, but the Creator of all. Make us gods. THE SAME. They say gods, because of the two pillars, etc., down to the pillar of fire went before the people by night.
7.42: 7.42 The host of heaven. The host of heaven is sometimes called the army of angels, but in this place he names the stars the host of heaven, since he immediately adds, the star of your god. In the book, etc. Although the prophets are many, yet one book is said to be, and among the Hebrews it is one book. Did you offer victims. RABANUS. Though from the necessity of serving God they made libations, yet in mind, etc., down to always in heart they returned to Egypt. It is asked how they did not offer to God, when it is read that they offered some things to God, not by will, but through fear of punishments? God, however, receives not the things offered but the will of those who offer.
7.43: 7.43 Figures, etc. RABANUS. The star of your god is Lucifer, to whom they assigned figures. The same gods were worshiped in figures and stars. THE SAME. Some thus say the star of your god, so that the word pertains to God, because they received not the Lord himself but his star. And I will carry you away. For these sacrileges you will be led captive beyond Babylon. The first martyr is not to be thought to have erred, who for what is written in the prophet, Beyond Damascus they were led, said, beyond Babylon: for he put the understanding rather than the word, because beyond Damascus they were led into Babylon, or beyond Babylon.
7.44: 7.44 The tabernacle. Because they said he acted against the holy place, he shows that he spoke no blasphemy against the holy place. According to the pattern. RABANUS. Which he had shown him on Sinai, because it was made according to the pattern, the tabernacle itself is shown to have been a pattern. THE SAME. Historically it is said with Jesus, because Moses was dead.
7.46: 7.46 To find a tabernacle. That is, the true temple, of which that was a figure, which was not to be changed in place, that is the Church, which he foresaw would be firm and unchangeable, of which the Apostle says: The sure foundation of God stands, 2 Timothy 2, 9. And elsewhere: For other foundation no man can lay but that which is laid, which is Christ Jesus, 1 Corinthians 3.
7.48: 7.48 But the Most High does not. RABANUS. From the saying of Solomon he convicts the Jews, etc., down to that he does not dwell in the temple of the Jews alone. As the prophet says, etc. Of the first tabernacle, which was a shadow and not the truth, he said first, afterwards he set the testimony of one speaking of the tabernacle which was more true. If I shall enter into the tabernacle of the Lord, etc., he set God at the last sentence. That in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may stand.
7.49: 7.49 Heaven is my. So he shows that he encompasses all things; hence elsewhere he asserts that he measures heaven with a span and holds the earth in his fist. And earth. By the example of the earth he designates every creature of the Creator.
7.51: 7.51 Stiff-necked. RABANUS. Cleared of the charge of which false witnesses accused him, he begins to rebuke the Jews, because he who is without crime is worthy of the office of teacher. And uncircumcised, etc. He shows them that the circumcision of which they boasted against the grace of the Gospel does not avail for salvation to those who had an unclean thought and hearing.
7.52: 7.52 Your fathers. RABANUS. Above he said our fathers, speaking to persuade, now rebuking he calls them fathers of those only whom they resemble in malice. And they killed. RABANUS. He sets three degrees of their malice: the first is that they resisted the Spirit; the second that they persecuted the prophets; the third that, their malice growing, they killed them.
7.55: 7.55 Standing. Immovably, because he is not to fall again, or the bearing of one helping, and judging injuries, and fighting for his servant is indicated. I see the heavens. RABANUS. About to depart from the earth, he saw the heavens opened, that he who despised earthly life for Christ may deserve the inheritance of heaven, and therefore in the passion itself he sees the reward. The Son of man. Since Christ is the Son of God, he preferred nevertheless to call himself Son of man, that the unbelief of the Jews may be confounded, who crucified him as mere man whom they would not believe to be God.
7.57: 7.57 And casting him out. RABANUS. In this they boasted of fulfilling the law. For Moses said of the blasphemer: Bring him forth out of the camp, and let the people stone him, Leviticus 24.
7.58: 7.58 Lord Jesus, receive my spirit, into the heaven which I see opened. Christ said to the Father: Father, into your hands I commend my spirit. Stephen, as servant to the Lord, Lord, etc. Because they know not. RABANUS. Many of them, by killing Stephen, thought they fulfilled the law, because they believed him a blasphemer. This also Christ had foretold: The hour comes, he said, that whoever kills you will think he does a service to God, John 16.
7.59: 7.59 He fell asleep. Beautifully it is said, he fell asleep, and not, he died, because he offered the sacrifice of love, and fell asleep in the hope of the resurrection. The saints do not die, because they are changed for the better, and temporal life is turned into eternal. And Saul, etc. He did not stone, indeed, but consented to the stoners. Whence he would have perished, if the grace of God and repentance had not come to his aid; because those who do and consent are worthy of death.
8.1: 8.1 In that day. RABANUS. On which Stephen was killed, not because it was done only then, but because from that day a great persecution began, one of the chiefs of the Church being killed. The Church. A gathering or congregation, or calling. They were scattered. This is what the Lord commanded: When they persecute you in this city, flee into another, Matthew 10. For it was done by his nod, that on the occasion of tribulation there might be a nursery of the Gospel.
8.2: 8.2 And devout men took care of Stephen, that is, God-fearing, either Christians who afterwards were scattered, or Jews fearing God though not yet Christians.
8.3: 8.3 Saul. RABANUS. From Saul the persecutor who was king of Israel of the tribe of Benjamin, of which Paul also was; for according to the custom of the ancients descendants take names from their forefathers. He laid waste. THE SAME. Like a wolf the flock, according to the prophecy of Jacob: Benjamin a ravenous wolf, in the morning shall devour the prey, and in the evening shall divide the spoils, Genesis 49. Dragging. He dragged, he did not kill, because perhaps the Lord held his hands, lest they be polluted with the blood of the innocent. Scattered. RABANUS. Though scattered by fear, they were yet steadfast in the preaching of the Gospel.
8.5: 8.5 Philip. He was of the number of those scattered, who first preached Christ in Samaria. A deacon, second from Stephen. He is told of as second after him, like an heir and of the same rank.
8.6: 8.6 They attended. RABANUS. They believed, hearing the words and seeing the signs. Two causes of faith: the words of preaching, and the signs of power. From the present chapter and the history of the Samaritan woman it is proved that the minds of this people were ready to believe, says Bede.
8.11: 8.11 With his magic. RABANUS. Magicians philosophize about particulars, about the nature of the world, the course of the stars, and their motions. Seducing. Leading apart and away from the truth, or turning to excess, or astonishment and wonder, by their tricks. Had bewitched. To bewitch is to make the rational mind absent.
8.12: 8.12 To Philip. RABANUS. Some say that this Philip was the apostle, and one of the twelve, but this does not seem true according to the sequence of this book. Of Jesus Christ. THE SAME. Of whom they were ignorant, or (as was said before) he preached the Trinity in the name of Jesus, and he who perfectly believes only one person of the Trinity cannot lack belief in the other two.
8.13: 8.13 Then Simon. THE SAME. Or he believed the Lord, by Philip's words and power, etc., down to having entered the Church fraudulently, steal baptism.
8.14: 8.14 They sent. Peter joins John with himself, because the virginity of the Church is pleasing and gratifying.
8.16: 8.16 In the name. It is not to be read thus, in the name of Jesus only, as though to exclude the other persons, but thus: they had only been baptized, etc., that is not yet confirmed. Jesus. Yet before, they believed in the Father and in the Holy Spirit, like other Jews. Or, full faith in one person confirms faith in the Trinity.
8.17: 8.17 They laid hands. BEDE. Philip, who was evangelizing Samaria, one of the seven, etc., down to when he gives the Spirit the Paraclete to the baptized.
8.19: 8.19 Power. RABANUS. Not only of baptizing in water and preaching, or working miracles which Philip had, but of laying hands on anyone, etc.
8.20: 8.20 Your money. Not ours, who do not desire it, but yours, which you compare with the Spirit, that you may sell it for him, and buy it with the Spirit. He wished therefore to buy the Spirit, that selling it to others he might receive more. Money. RABANUS. From this an example is taken that the alms of the lost are not to be received. The apostles, unwilling to take money, say, be with you, that is keep your own, and this, to perdition, that, money unjustly gathered, you may suffer eternal punishment.
8.22: 8.22 Repent. For the covetousness, and the perverse sense by which you thought commerce could be made of the Spirit. RABANUS. That all may see what you are. Not that Peter did not know he would not repent, but because it is right for all to preach, he does his office, that he may be inexcusable. Before all he is also rebuked that they may not be further deceived by him. Pray God. To whom the heart is open, of whom the Prophet: How good is the God of Israel, Psalm 72; whom no one can deceive, because the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee from the deceitful, Wisdom 1.
8.24: 8.24 Pray. Because of despair he does not himself dare to pray, but asks the apostles to pray for him, nor dares he pray for himself who does not believe he will be heard. He also speaks falsely to the apostles. What you have said. Not what he believed, but like an unbeliever he imputes to them what is to come.
8.26: 8.26 And an angel. After the return of the apostles, the history of Philip is woven in. To the way, etc. For the way descends, and one goes down by the way from the nature of the place.
8.27: 8.27 An Ethiopian. By nature and by merit. For Ethiopian is dark. Hence: Ethiopia shall stretch out her hands to God, Psalm 67. Powerful, etc. BEDE. The queen of the Ethiopians sending ahead the treasurer, etc., down to Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline your ear, Psalm 44, etc. Of Candace the queen. It was the custom of that region to be ruled by women, and they were called Candaces.
8.28: 8.28 He was returning. He began to return reading Isaiah. Wherever in the New Testament the beginning of salvation is told, the testimony is taken from Isaiah, which is interpreted salvation of the Lord.
8.30: 8.30 Do you think you understand, etc. RABANUS. They know each other's tongues, either through the teaching of the eunuch or through the spirit of Philip.
8.31: 8.31 How, etc. Here he rebukes the boldness of those who think they can understand divine Scripture without a teacher.
8.33: 8.33 In humility. BEDE. For the judge of all did not find the truth of judgment, but without any fault of his own, by the sedition of the Jews and the voice of Pilate, he was condemned. In humility. RABANUS. By the passion in which he humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, Philippians 2. Shall be taken. The second man from heaven, heavenly, separated in holiness from earthly things, or, he will pass from life to death.
8.35: 8.35 He opened. RABANUS. He opened the treasure of knowledge. Or he opened his mouth, that the Spirit may speak in him, according to that: Open your mouth wide and I will fill it, Psalm 80. Mystically, Philip opened the mouth of the Church, that from this he may be preached to the Gentiles whom they did not know before. He preached. He resolved the question of the one asking: Of whom does the prophet say this? He shows, moreover, that it was prophesied of Jesus.
8.36: 8.36 To a certain water. For to this the preaching had led, that he should need water, who had heard of baptism on the way.
8.37: 8.37 If you believe. RABANUS. He was not ignorant of his faith, but wanted a manifest confession, that an example of asking and confessing might be given to those who are to baptize and to be baptized.
8.39: 8.39 The Spirit of the Lord. RABANUS. Or the Spirit rushed upon him mightily, as upon the apostles, etc., down to upon whom the Spirit had descended?
8.40: 8.40 Was found. By men, who in the rapture was not found, because he walked in solitude, or by excessive swiftness. Caesarea. BEDE. He means Caesarea of Palestine, where below he is described to have had a house, which is shown to this day, and also the chamber of his four daughters, virgins who prophesied.
9.1: 9.1 And Saul. He returns to what he had said above: Saul still laid waste the Church. Of threats, etc. Terrifying with threats he afflicted those present with slaughter: it is doubtful whether he killed or scourged, or did both. Breathing. He breathes in the manner of fire, himself not incited by another, he inflamed others.
9.4: 9.4 And falling. Terrified, he fled to the ground, or as if adoring he falls on his face. Why do you, etc. BEDE. He does not say: Why do you persecute, etc., down to As long as you did it to one of these least, you did it to me, Matthew 25.
9.5: 9.5 I am Jesus. He does not call himself God or Son of God, but, he says, take up the weaknesses of my humility, and lay down the scales of your pride.
9.7: 9.7 Arise. Work readily like an ox, and be a teacher of the Church. In the law it is written: You shall not muzzle the ox that treads out the grain, 1 Corinthians 9. Enter. RABANUS. About to enter the city he is terrified, lest he bring sadness to the saints; then the Lord is bidden to enter, that he may learn the faith which he had attacked. And it shall be told. An example of learning is given, and pride is rebuked, that no one think another unworthy by whom he is taught what he does not know.
9.8: 9.8 His eyes being opened. RABANUS. It is shown to him in the body what he had before suffered in the soul. For as an open eye without sight, so the law is useless without the faith of Christ. BEDE. He could not see well again with his eyes unless he had first been blinded, and, shutting out his own wisdom, which is troubled, committed himself to faith.
9.9: 9.9 And he was. RABANUS. Here a pattern is given to penitents, that they begin from three days, and by this three days the degree of catechumens is also dedicated. Three days. It appears that for three days, blinded, he awaited the light of grace, not idle in torpor, but enlightened by God he searched heavenly things. It is credible that even at that time he was taught the dispensation of the Gospel. Not seeing. Because he did not believe that God had conquered death by rising on the third day, he is instructed by his own example, who changed the darkness of three days into light restored. He did not eat. RABANUS. This had happened to his soul, which had not the inner food and drink. From the fasting and thirst of the body it is shown that the needy soul must be satisfied.
9.10: 9.10 Ananias. THE SAME. It is a mark of familiarity to be called by one's own name.
9.11: 9.11 Into the street. THE SAME. Streets are called fields, or those next to cities, or next to oneself within the city.
9.15: 9.15 Go, etc. He is not to be feared as a persecutor, but embraced as a brother: because he is ready to bear the evils which he inflicted on the saints.
9.17: 9.17 He entered. The prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled: The wolf shall dwell with the lamb, that is, Saul with Ananias.
9.18: 9.18 There fell, etc. BEDE. The serpent's body is covered with scales, etc., down to that he received light in the mind. RABANUS. That the scales fall is a likeness of the inner sight renewed from the veil of the law.
9.20: 9.20 And immediately. He fulfills the word of the Lord who says: He that will come after me, let him deny himself, Luke 9, etc.
9.21: 9.21 Is not. RABANUS. He gives an example of not being ashamed, where truth can change its sentences.
9.24: 9.24 They watched. Not the Jews, but the citizens with their king Aretas, as he himself writes to the Galatians. For the Gentiles agreed with the Jews in the persecution of Christians.
9.26: 9.26 And when he was come. Not as soon as he was baptized: did he come to Jerusalem to the apostles, but (as he writes to the Galatians) first he went into Arabia, and from there returned to Damascus; then after three years he came to Jerusalem to see Peter, etc. Then, as Luke testifies, he came into the parts of Syria and Cilicia.
9.27: 9.27 Barnabas. BEDE. He was a Cypriot by race, a Levite, who is mentioned above to have brought the price of a field to the feet of the apostles.
9.29: 9.29 With the Greeks. Greek Jews are so called because they were born among the Greeks in the dispersion.
9.30: 9.30 Caesarea. Caesarea Philippi is a city of Syria. Tarsus is a city of Cilicia.
9.31: 9.31 The Church. Such things, as was said above, are often interposed at the end and beginning of narrations, for the praise of the apostles and of the ecclesiastical faith. And with the comfort. Comfort is given in labor, whence it is clear that the Church was being tried.
9.33: 9.33 By name Aeneas. RABANUS. Aeneas signifies the human race languishing, etc., down to he who is sick with the pleasure of the flesh and the delight of the world.
9.34: 9.34 Arise. Him whom he had cured of paralysis he bade arise and make his own bed, suggesting that he who had received faith in the heart should not only shake off torpor, but also prepare works in which to rest.
9.35: 9.35 Lydda and Sharon. Two cities were turned to God, for that is why powers were wrought in them.
9.36: 9.36 By name Tabitha. RABANUS. Tabitha is translated from Hebrew into Latin as Dorcas, or Damula (the little doe), as is found in some copies. Dorcas. Allegorically: Dorcas is a roe or little doe: it signifies a soul lofty by zeal of virtue, but contemptible in the opinion of men. Luke, by setting down the interpretation of the name, signifies that a mystery is in it. These animals dwelling on mountains see keenly: hence from the keenness of sight they are called dorcades in Greek. So the lofty by merit of works look intently upward, and watch circumspectly over themselves, live simply with a discerning step of work, walk as with a cloven hoof, ruminate the word of God by assiduous meditation.
9.39: 9.39 In the upper chamber. RABANUS. She is placed in a higher place, either for the height of her merit, or for the sublimity of the miracle which was to be done upon her.
9.40: 9.40 Putting them all out. THE SAME. After the example of Christ raising the daughter of the ruler of the synagogue this was done, to avoid elation, or lest the unworthy see the sign. He opened. BEDE. The order of those rising is right, that first she open the eyes of the mind, afterwards, the voice of Peter being recognized, sit up, recover the light of her lost circumspection, that she may live for the teaching of those who help. She opened her eyes. These are the three degrees of resuscitation.
9.41: 9.41 And giving. Her hand touched by Peter, Tabitha rises, because a soul languishing in sins recovers in no better order than by the examples of the saints.
10.1: 10.1 And there was a man, etc. RABANUS. For the merit of perfection and manly work this centurion is called a man, according to that: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. Cornelius. BEDE. He did not reach virtues by faith, but reached faith by virtues. GREGORY. Cornelius, whose alms before baptism, the angel testifying, etc., down to in faith it is made solid by works.
10.2: 10.2 Religious, etc. RABANUS. All these by the good of nature, etc., down to without male seed, that is, he is believed to have conceived by the teaching of a master.
10.3: 10.3 He saw. RABANUS. Not in the night, not in sleep, because the Gentiles with a gross sense, etc., down to as was shown before in the example of Peter and John. An angel of God. THE SAME. Not of Satan. In this the apostles are excused who preach to the Gentiles and baptize them: for how could that be envied of a man which was made manifest by an angel? Coming in, to himself perhaps, calling him, and an occasion of excusing is given to Peter when the Jews disputed against him and said: Why did you go in to men having foreskin? Acts 11, etc. Cornelius. Familiarity is shown, by which the name of a Gentile man was inserted in the knowledge of the angels.
10.5: 10.5 And now send men, etc. RABANUS. Here the repayment begins, that he who is merciful, God may have mercy on you, because: Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy, Matthew 5. Joppa. THE SAME. A city of the land of promise nearest the Tyrrhenian sea, and situated on its eastern shore, into which Jonah going down entered a ship to flee.
10.6: 10.6 He lodges, etc. Peter lodges in the house of Simon, that is, of the obedient, who is a tanner, because the teacher of the Church gladly dwells where there are obedient ones, who chastise the body and bring it into servitude, having crossed the waves of the age with liberty of mind. For by constancy of faith they despise the fleeting glory of the world and its terrors.
10.7: 10.7 And when he was departed. RABANUS. He does not say, when Cornelius had awakened, because to him neither by a dream nor in an ecstasy but manifestly the angel was seen. A soldier. THE SAME. He does not say household fearing the Lord, because at the beginning he had said that he was religious, fearing the Lord with all his house.
10.9: 10.9 As they drew near, etc. Another reading: They appearing, namely those who were sent by Cornelius, that is, so near that they could be seen from the house of Simon the tanner. RABANUS. For, to the upper parts, another reading has, to the upper chamber, and well: because the Gentile people are as the upper house: the Synagogue is below, because immersed in the world. Saying, to the upper parts, he signified the Church, having left the covetousness of earthly things, about to have her conversation in heaven. At the sixth hour Peter among prayers hungers, for the salvation of the world, obviously, which Jesus came in the sixth age of the world to seek and to save: which he indicated when at the same hour he sat upon the well of Samaria.
10.10: 10.10 When he was hungry. RABANUS. He hungers, sympathizing with the salvation of the Gentiles, which is now shown in the vision, which was therefore seen at the sixth hour, because it was done in the sixth age of the world.
10.11: 10.11 Heaven opened. BEDE. The opening of heaven is the revelation of heavenly sacraments soon to be given to the Gentiles. He designates in this that the heavens are opened to the Gentiles, and the entrance to be laid open. A certain vessel. THE SAME. That vessel designates the Church, etc., down to by whom the Church, imbued with heavenly gift, is lifted up. A linen sheet. For the Church, for the whiteness of holiness, and the mortification of the flesh. From heaven to earth. RABANUS. From this we are admonished that where our head and root is (of which we are branches), thither the anchor of our hope should reach.
10.12: 10.12 All the four-footed beasts. All the nations to believe and to be taken into the unity of the body of Christ, that all may become his members.
10.13: 10.13 Kill. Cleanse, mortify, and sacrifice, that you may make victims to God, that, rescued from oldness, they may pass into newness.
10.14: 10.14 I have never eaten, etc. BEDE. He who eats food placed outside carries it into his own body. He commanded therefore the Gentiles, by unbelief placed outside, to be inserted into the fellowship of the Church (which Peter signifies). THE SAME. Peter thought the Gentiles unclean, etc., down to but bind in the love of God alone.
10.21: 10.21 Going down. BEDE. To descend from the roof, and to go to preach, he is bidden, etc., down to But the conversation of the saints is in heaven, Philippians 3. Behold I, etc. He shows that he knows their coming, giving also an example of humility, leaving aside circumlocution of words. What is the cause, etc. The Spirit said the soldiers were there, and was silent about the reason for which they had come, because, to preserve humility, at times the spirit of prophecy touches the mind in part, and in part does not touch.
10.22: 10.22 He received answer. To his alms and prayers the Lord answered through an angel. Into his house. By this they persuade, because the angel commanded to enter his house, though he was a Gentile.
10.23: 10.23 Bringing them in, etc. Here the communion of the apostles with the Gentiles begins, because he had gone down to those who had heard from the angel the command that they should enter the house of a Gentile, therefore he received the Gentiles in hospitality.
10.24: 10.24 Having called together his kinsmen, etc. A twofold cause of the calling together: nearness of kinship, and friendship.
10.27: 10.27 And speaking, etc. BEDE. Holiness of action deserved communion of equality, as in the fault of Ananias and Sapphira the zeal of his vengeance opened his power.
10.30: 10.30 And behold a man, etc. He does not say an angel, so alien was he from pride, and he says: Cornelius, your prayer is heard, and your alms are had in remembrance before God. In the sight of God. RABANUS. In the Greek, In the sight of God we are present. This is rightly said by him who was ready to obey God, believing him to be present everywhere.
10.34: 10.34 God is no respecter of persons, etc. BEDE. It is clear that God is no respecter of persons, etc., down to but all believers would receive.
10.37: 10.37 You know, etc. RABANUS. It is to be read thus: You know Jesus as John preached: Jesus of Nazareth, how he anointed him, etc. Or: this John preached, that he anointed him, not indeed in an earthly manner, but with the Spirit and the power of signs.
10.38: 10.38 Who went about, etc. In the Greek is added, for forty days, not that they ate and drank with him every day, for it would be contrary to John, who interposes eight days in which he was not seen by them, that he might be manifested on the third, and for as many days he fasted before his death, needing food, which he ate after the resurrection no longer needing food. He fasted before death, that we might abstain from the desires of this age. He ate, teaching by this that he is with us to the consummation of the age. Fasting is in the struggle, for he who is in the contest abstains from all things. Food is in the hope of peace, which will be perfect when this mortal shall put on immortality. We, when we walk the way of the Lord, fast from the vanity of the age, and are refreshed by the future promise. RABANUS.
