For forty days, not continually, but at certain times made within that number of forty days.
10.41: 10.41 And drank. BEDE. Here Peter explains what is passed over in silence in the Gospel, that after the resurrection he drank with Christ, unless perhaps we believe it indicated there, where he says: Until I drink it with you in the kingdom of my Father, Matthew 26.
10.45: 10.45 The Spirit. The Spirit is the gift of God, inasmuch as he is given to those who through him love God; but in himself he is God, even if given to none, coeternal with the Father and the Son. Nor, because they give and he is given, is he less than they. For he is so given as the gift of God that he gives himself as God: for the Spirit breathes where he will, John 3.
10.47: 10.47 Can any man, etc. As if God gave first what is greater and inverted the order, can anyone forbid what is less? You have come for this, that you may be witnesses, therefore judge.
10.48: 10.48 In the name of Christ. Though the rule of the Church is that baptism be given in the name of the Trinity, Luke nevertheless testifies it is given in the name of Jesus Christ. Which Ambrose resolving says that through the unity of the name the mystery is made full, because he who says Christ designates also the Father by whom the Son is, and the Holy Spirit: he who says Father shows likewise the Son and the Spirit: and he who names the Spirit names the Father from whom the Spirit proceeds, and the Son, whose Spirit he also is. Hence, that authority may be joined to reason, he is also baptized in the Spirit, according to that: You shall be baptized in the Holy Spirit, Acts 11, and the Apostle: In one Spirit we have been baptized, 1 Corinthians 12.
11.6: 11.6 The four-footed beasts of the earth, etc. RABANUS. I marvel that some interpret this about foods, etc., down to expounded the mystery of this vision.
11.18: 11.18 Therefore to the Gentiles also, etc. This is what is read in Job: From the north gold shall come, and to God a fearful praise, because first the splendor of faith arose in the cold breast of the Gentiles, and for the same unexpected faith Judea glorifies God, trembling.
11.19: 11.19 And they indeed, etc. He returns to what he had said: Therefore those who were dispersed went about preaching the word. The narration is interposed, however, about Philip, Peter, John, Paul.
11.20: 11.20 And there were some. RABANUS. Not of those who had been scattered from Jerusalem, but, etc., down to were living among the Greeks in the dispersion.
11.21: 11.21 And a great number. BEDE. Now after the revelation of the evangelical sheet (in which the holy animals would rest in heavenly hope) the Church began to grow, when through foreign provinces, islands and cities the Gospel is preached not only to Jews, but also to Gentiles.
11.22: 11.22 And they sent Barnabas. RABANUS. Barnabas, manly in goodness. Barnabas is often praised in this book, lest it be believed that through unworthiness of merit he lacked apostleship, who afterwards was ordained by the apostles an apostle of the Gentiles.
11.23: 11.23 And he exhorted, etc. He changed or added nothing, but taught perseverance, because the faith in them was true and full.
11.25: 11.25 To Tarsus. For it was said above that the brethren brought him by night to Caesarea and sent him to Tarsus. To seek Saul. Behold the goodness of Barnabas, who does not presume to teach the people alone, but seeks a partner in the apostleship.
11.26: 11.26 Disciples, Christians. In these, etc. The disciples seem in this not to have kept the commandment of God saying: Be not solicitous for tomorrow, Matthew 6. But it is established that he does not disapprove this, if anyone provides for these things in a human way, but does not serve God for them, so as in his work to look not to the kingdom of God but to temporal things. To this rule therefore this precept is reduced, that in provision for these we look to the kingdom of God: but in God's warfare we do not think on these things. Prophets. RABANUS. Of whom it is said: And your sons shall prophesy, Joel 2. It is the praise of Antioch that many perfect men assembled there.
12.4: 12.4 Four quaternions. A quaternion is called the chief of four soldiers. For as a centurion has a hundred, so a quaternion has four soldiers under him. Willing, etc. RABANUS. For the grace would be greater if the Jews themselves killed him, because he was a prince, not Herod himself, as with James.
12.6: 12.6 The soldiers, bound, etc. RABANUS. Four difficulties heap up the custody: soldiers, chains, prison, keepers.
12.7: 12.7 A light. A sign of the presence of the angel of God, whose presence gave light to Peter alone, and did not shine on others. And striking. RABANUS. The angel, taking a body from the air, could have a bodily touch.
12.11: 12.11 Coming to himself. He returned from the summit of contemplation to that which was before in common understanding.
12.13: 12.13 A girl came forward, etc. And the Lord who came out of the tomb a woman first of all announced to the disciples, that where sin abounded, grace might superabound.
12.15: 12.15 It is his angel. JEROME. Great is the dignity of souls: that each from the origin of birth has an angel appointed for his keeping. THE SAME. That each of us has angels, etc., down to these are they who ascend and descend upon the Son of man.
12.17: 12.17 To be silent, etc. Until he should tell the power: or he bids them be silent, lest by the cry of the rejoicing his coming be known in the city.
12.23: 12.23 Immediately, etc. As he did not shrink from the impiety of unlawful flattery, looking back a little later he saw the angel hanging over and pressing on his head, and felt him at once the minister of his destruction, whom before he had known as provider of goods. Then, tormented seven days continually with pain of the belly, he violently broke off his life.
13.1: 13.1 Now there were in the Church, etc. The same were prophets and teachers. Or, some of them were prophets, others teachers. Niger. RABANUS. From the color, if it is Latin. Or, ascending, is interpreted, if Hebrew.
13.4: 13.4 Sent by the Holy Spirit. RABANUS. Dismissed by men, they are soon sent by the Holy Spirit to Seleucia. He was leader of their journey, who separated them from the rest. They departed to Seleucia. THE SAME. In some copies is found: They departed to Seleucia, which is Salamis; but there are two names of one city.
13.7: 13.7 Sergius Paulus. Sergius and Paulus are two names of one man.
13.8: 13.8 Elymas. RABANUS. Elymas, according to some, is interpreted measure of my God, or Magus, and therefore he resisted. To turn away. THE SAME. He wished to turn him who had begun to be converted from faith to transgression, according to his name.
13.9: 13.9 Saul. THE SAME. Saul is interpreted Temptation of one looking back, or security, or wonderful. Who is also Paul. BEDE. From Sergius Paulus the proconsul (whom he subdued to the faith) he obtained the name of Paul. Fittingly the apostle of the Gentiles obtains his name from a Gentile. RABANUS. The apostle was called Paul from Sergius Paulus, etc., down to I am the least of the apostles, 1 Corinthians 15.
13.11: 13.11 And now, etc. You shall be blind, etc. It behooved Paul to work miracles for the consummation of the apostleship, whom the Lord had chosen, long kicking against the goads.
13.14: 13.14 Antioch of Pisidia. RABANUS. To distinguish it from the other Antioch, as is believed; but by many it is thought to be the same. They sat. THE SAME. As about to hear the law, not to preach. Behold an example of humility.
13.19: 13.19 The land of Canaan, etc. RABANUS. That is of promise, which was therefore (as most think) given to Israel, etc., down to and therefore deserved to be cursed.
13.20: 13.20 He gave, etc. The time of the judges passes to prove the patience of God.
13.26: 13.26 To you. RABANUS. To the Jews. I am not sent but to the sheep that are lost of the house of Israel, Matthew 15. Or to you, who are dispersed, because (as follows) the inhabitants of Jerusalem rejected it.
13.27: 13.27 Judging. THE SAME. That Jesus was guilty of death. Or, judging the voices of the prophets, that is not believing: for he who detracts from his brother detracts from the law and judges the law, how much more those detracting from Christ? The holy things of David the faithful. BEDE. Isaiah foretasting the mysteries of the New Testament says: I will make with you an everlasting covenant, the sure mercies of David. In the Hebrew: And I will strike with you an everlasting covenant, the faithful mercies of David.
13.35: 13.35 You will not give, etc. THE SAME. After the resurrection he does not die, death shall no more have dominion over him, and therefore he says the holy faithful things, that is incorrupt and eternally abiding.
13.41: 13.41 Behold, you despisers. In the Greek: Hear, you despisers, and look and be destroyed. Wonder. RABANUS. Join thus: Wonder and be scattered by the Assyrians and Chaldeans, lastly by the Romans, because I work a work of each vengeance. You will not believe, etc. Or because of the greatness of each vengeance, they are said not to believe until they have been fulfilled.
13.43: 13.43 And of those who worship. THE SAME. Well is it read worshiping God, as in the Greek. It signifies, however, those who by nature were Gentiles but in religion Jews, in Greek called proselytes.
13.46: 13.46 First. THE SAME. First Jesus came to heal the daughter of the ruler, but the woman suffering a flow of blood snatched away the healing. Of eternal life. Not because they knew eternal life to be what they rejected, but the apostles spoke from their own sense and their faith.
13.47: 13.47 For so, etc. THE SAME. The prophecy is an immovable command for us: first it is said, then the testimony of the Prophet is brought in, to the person of the Father speaking to the Son. I have set you. He does not say, I have set you (plural), because what is said to Christ pertains to the apostles, who are his members. I have set you for a light to the Gentiles. BEDE. This was said specially to Christ, and yet the apostles think the same said to themselves, because they are his members: as on account of the union of the same body it was said, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? etc.
13.48: 13.48 Ordained. The order here is that after present labors and mortification of the flesh, life follows.
13.50: 13.50 Religious women. RABANUS. Either of the Jews who kept the religion of the law, or of the Gentiles beginning to save religion.
13.51: 13.51 Shaking off the dust, etc. According to the precept of the Gospel, the dust is shaken off in testimony that they made the labor vain. RABANUS. Deservedly the dust is shaken off, because in the judgment they will be cast out by Christ like the dust which the wind drives from the face of the earth, Psalm 1. But if they received the apostles, they would loose their feet, that is their senses, from the dust, that is vices.
14.6: 14.6 They fled. RABANUS. The flight of the apostles was no more from fear than from love of the word of God. And all, etc. What follows in the Greek: But God made peace, some Latin codices lack.
14.10: 14.10 They lifted up. RABANUS. In this petulance is noted. Or, the sentence was higher than their barbarous tongue and ignorant of the one God.
14.12: 14.12 Garlands. THE SAME. That he might adorn the front of the temple according to the rite of the Gentiles, or place them upon them (as about to sacrifice to gods). It was the custom of the Gentiles that those sacrificing to the honor of their gods took garlands, the victims being crowned at the same time.
14.16: 14.16 Filling with food, etc. THE SAME. He speaks of carnal things, because gladness is from foods and wine which makes glad the heart of man.
14.18: 14.18 They dragged. THE SAME. To stone him as a corpse, of this he himself to the Corinthians: Once I was stoned, 2 Corinthians 11, etc.
14.21: 14.21 To continue in the faith. THE SAME. Against many tribulations: because a multitude of tribulations demands perseverance of faith. That through many tribulations. Labor is put first, then the entrance of the kingdom is preached, because the hope of the reward is the solace of labor.
15.2: 15.2 Sedition. By Paul and Barnabas, against those who said these things. They appointed. RABANUS. Namely those who had come down from Judea, etc., down to is proved to have come to the faith.
15.6: 15.6 And the apostles came together. THE SAME. Here an example is given of holding councils to discern what is necessary to the faith.
15.7: 15.7 By my mouth. THE SAME. Not by another of the apostles, as if he said: I who first preached to the Gentiles, first shake off from them the yoke of the law. For none of the apostles preached to the eunuch: but Philip the deacon, and he was filled with the free gift.
15.9: 15.9 Purifying by faith. CHRYSOSTOM. By faith alone, he says, they obtained those things, and not by works or circumcision. For they do not say these things only to give account for the Gentiles, but also desiring to draw them from the law: but they do not yet say this.
15.12: 15.12 And all the multitude held their peace. The order of speaking or of speakers is to be noted, for they are silent for each speaker, first for Peter.
15.13: 15.13 And after, etc. CHRYSOSTOM. He was bishop of the Church of Jerusalem, etc., down to where he also puts an end to works.
15.16: 15.16 I will return and rebuild, etc. I will return to the Gentiles, of whom he had before said that they enter their own ways, to confirm which sense James brought the testimony. This testimony plainly agrees with the words of Simon. RABANUS. The shadow of the law, corrupted by the traditions of the Pharisees, by the Lord revealing, that is the Lord appearing in the flesh, is by grace raised up, that not only Jews but also Gentiles may seek his name.
15.17: 15.17 Upon whom my name is called. THE SAME. According to that: The priests shall call upon my name over the children of Israel, Numbers 6; and elsewhere: Moses and Aaron among his priests, Psalm 98, etc. Is called. For the future, in the prophetic manner.
15.19: 15.19 I judge. RABANUS. It was right to judge what is confirmed by the testimony of three, of the two apostles and of the prophets.
15.20: 15.20 And from things strangled. What is strangled is carrion, of which Ezekiel says: The priests shall not eat anything dead or torn by a beast, of birds or cattle, Ezekiel 4. This precept it is fitting for those to keep who are anointed with spiritual oil, that they not eat that whose blood has not been poured out, which the epistle of the apostles decreed to be kept. And from blood. RABANUS. From the shedding of human blood, etc., down to but that they be chaste and abstain.
15.22: 15.22 Then it pleased. THE SAME. Peter speaking, Barnabas and Paul narrating, James bishop of Jerusalem judging, the sentence deservedly pleased. It pleased to send to Antioch. Legates sent by Christ can send legates.
15.23: 15.23 The apostles and elders. The common title of the apostles is put first, lest any occasion of dissension be left. To the brethren of the Gentiles. RABANUS. The first benefit of the style is that the apostles call the Gentiles brethren, that is sons of the one God. Greeting. An ellipsis, because every word is too narrow for the breadth of charity, and therefore no word is put, so that all good things together may be understood to be wished for them.
15.24: 15.24 Subverting souls. In the Greek: Subverting your souls, saying: You must be circumcised, and keep the law, to whom we gave no commandment.
15.28: 15.28 It seemed good. That is it pleased. To the Holy Spirit. Who as arbiter of his own power breathes where he will, and says what he will. To the Holy Spirit. RABANUS. And to us in a human sense indeed, but sound. And to us. Not however by our will alone, but by the instinct of the same Spirit. Than these necessary. RABANUS. Those things are necessary without which there is no salvation, but circumcision is not necessary: and the things which you do not wish done to you, do not do to others.
15.29: 15.29 That you abstain, etc. TERTULLIAN. Therefore since both kinds, etc., down to whose cleanness pertains more to God than that of the bowels.
15.34: 15.34 But it seemed good. RABANUS. It is the matter of the coming sermon: But Judas alone went to Jerusalem.
15.39: 15.39 Dissension. They did not offend in this, because not every emotion is a sin, but the irrational one, and that which is not rightly made. Taking Mark. He was joined to Barnabas by the bond of kinship, whence they are read to have been cousins. Barnabas, dismissed by Paul, returned to his native island, and nonetheless exercised the work of the Gospel enjoined on him.
15.40: 15.40 Having chosen Silas. RABANUS. The Lord made him remain for this, according to that: It seemed good to Silas to remain there, that he might cooperate with Paul as Mark with Barnabas. For there was divine counsel in this.
16.1: 16.1 A widow's son. RABANUS. Or of Judea. That she was a Jewess by race appears from his saying that he was born of a Gentile father.
16.3: 16.3 And circumcised him. THE SAME. He circumcised Timothy for the scandal of the Jews, lest he seem to condemn the law of Moses, but not impose it as unnecessary on the Gentiles. Titus he did not circumcise, lest the Gentiles take occasion of being circumcised from him. And what is it that he says: But because of false brethren brought in, etc.
16.4: 16.4 To keep the decrees which were. THE SAME. They did not preach what they themselves had done, but what the apostles had decreed for the will of God. And it is an example of teaching rightly even what you have not done. In figure of this deed the priests were clothed in breeches, as about to sow the work but not as about to do it.
16.5: 16.5 And the churches indeed, etc. THE SAME. This has been often explained in the above chapters, when we said that by a sentence of this sort the preceding narration is closed, and the beginning of the following is made.
16.7: 16.7 They attempted to go. THE SAME. The apostles are permitted to will, but not to go, etc., down to Luke in Bithynia, etc.
16.9: 16.9 A man of Macedonia. The angel of that nation likened to a Macedonian man, by property of language, or special form, or the judgment of the word. Help us. RABANUS. This was said from the person of the man, for angels do not need human help. Or the angel says this on account of those over whom he presides, that they may be baptized and saved. Help us. It shows that the Macedonians or angels are inspired by God, or that some teachers began to be taught.
16.11: 16.11 Samothrace. Thrace, Neapolis and Philippi are cities.
16.12: 16.12 Some, conferring. In some books is found: Conferring the word of the Lord on the sabbath day.
16.14: 16.14 A seller of purple. A queen clothed in royal purple, or a weaver of purple, or selling purple, signifies the Church, which sells purple while she sheds blood for Christ, that she may be able to buy life. Purple rightly designates blood by color and nature, because it is made from the blood of shellfish. Lydia compelled the apostle with his companions to enter her house: because the Church with devout heart received the preaching rejected by the Jews.
16.15: 16.15 She constrained us. RABANUS. Here an example is given, or two examples are given: one of constraining guests, the other of entering the houses of the newly converted.
16.17: 16.17 Following Paul. THE SAME. Although she had met them, she cries not in the face, but after them, the woman preserving modesty.
16.23: 16.23 They cast them into prison. THE SAME. By this the power of the liberator is greater. To the same end what follows looks: He put them into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks.
16.25: 16.25 And at midnight, etc. One must pray at midnight, and in dangers the diligence of prayer must be kept.
16.26: 16.26 There was a great earthquake, etc. The devotion of the praying and the power of prayer is expressed, because while they sing hymns in prison, their praise moves the earth: shakes the foundations of the prison, opens the doors, looses the chains of the bound.
16.29: 16.29 He fell down, etc. RABANUS. On account of power and knowledge: power, because by the earthquake the doors were opened: knowledge, because Paul knew why he wished to kill himself: therefore before all he fell at the feet of Paul and Silas.
16.33: 16.33 He washed their stripes. BEDE. A beautiful variety of things. He to whom he washed the stripes of the wound, through them lost the stripes of crime. Immediately. RABANUS. The swiftness of obedience is signified. The grace of the Holy Spirit knows no slow efforts.
16.34: 16.34 And when he had brought them, he set a table before them, etc. THE SAME. An excellent example of both: the entering of the house, and the setting of the table.
17.4: 17.4 And of the worshiping Gentiles. That is, both of those who had changed Gentile rite for Judaism, and of those who had remained Gentiles, many flocked to Christ. RABANUS. The first cause of malice is that these are of the common people; the second that they were also wicked beyond the common people.
17.6: 17.6 They dragged Jason. BEDE. In the Greek: Jason and certain other brethren. Hence it is to be understood that Jason was a brother and a believer.
17.7: 17.7 Another king. RABANUS. Besides Caesar. This was against the decree of Caesar, whence in the Gospel: Everyone who makes himself a king contradicts Caesar, John 18. The apostles, however, contradicted that Christ is king of the Jews, that is of the confessing, whence the Jews also accused Christ himself.
17.13: 17.13 By Paul. Who was the leader of the word: and therefore afterwards he alone was sent off, that he might go from Macedonia to the sea.
17.15: 17.15 They departed. RABANUS. From Athens those brethren who had conducted Paul departed. Some think it was said of Silas and Timothy, that they departed from Macedonia to Paul.
17.18: 17.18 Epicureans. THE SAME. They are so called from their founder, who is said to have been an asserter of pleasure. Stoics, in Greek; in Latin elements; who contended that sins are equal, that is every sin uniform. What does this seed-picker want. A seed-picker is one who sows a word; or seed-picker, that is a talker; because the word of God is seed; hence: If we have sown to you, etc. AUGUSTINE. We read that the apostle Paul was called a sower of words, which was said by mockers, but is not to be rejected by believers; for he was a sower of words, but a reaper of morals. And we, though little ones and not to be compared with him, in the field of God (which is your heart) sow the word of God, awaiting rich harvest, or fruit from your morals. Others. RABANUS. They heard from the Jews that the name of demons is abominable, and therefore compare the doctrine of Paul to this abomination; or they are Jews who say this, that is Sadducees.
17.19: 17.19 To the Areopagus. RABANUS. It is the name of a court at Athens, called from the idol of Mars, which among them is called Arios.
17.22: 17.22 Men of Athens, etc. What you worship in ignorance, this I proclaim. He answers what they had said or put forward: You bring some strange things, as if to say: The new things that I bring you have among your old ones. He says this to persuade them, lest they reject his words as new. To the unknown God. RABANUS. That is, to the true God, whom no one knows as he is, etc., down to which is passed over in silence, or it was simply written: To the unknown God.
17.24: 17.24 God, who made the world. Note the order of this discussion, because first he teaches that there is one God, author of the world and of all things, in whom we live, and move, and are, of whose race we are: so that he is shown to be loved not only for light and life, but also for kinship of race.
17.26: 17.26 Of one, every nation of men. In the Greek: of one blood, because blood designates the offspring of flesh, and through flesh man is understood.
17.28: 17.28 For in him we live. AUGUSTINE. Because it is he who works in us that we live and move and are, etc., down to for what is not from him of whom it is said: From him, and through him, and in him are all things, Romans 2? As some also of your poets. To those who did not receive the prophets, he speaks not the testimony of Moses, not of Isaiah, or of any of the prophets, but of their own authors, setting a verse of Aratus, and from the falsehoods of those whom they could not contradict he preserves and confirms his own truth. For of him, etc. This testimony is taken from the poet Aratus, not from the divine page, lest he seem to bring in new things.
17.29: 17.29 Being therefore the offspring, etc., we ought not. RABANUS. Man is in the middle, having God above him, gold and silver with other such things below, which ought not to be compared to him.
17.30: 17.30 God, looking down. THE SAME. That is, pardoning as venial, and then looking down, that is judging unworthy of his notice.
17.31: 17.31 Giving faith to all. THE SAME. By the example of his resurrection: or he has appointed to judge, and after that it is to be joined thus, giving faith to all that they will rise.
17.34: 17.34 Dionysius. BEDE. This is the Dionysius who, afterwards ordained bishop of the Corinthians, ruled the Church well, and for its profit left also many volumes, taking his surname from the place over which he presided. The Areopagus is the court of Athens, drawing its name from Mars, who in Greek is called Arios, pagus, village.
18.2: 18.2 Because Claudius had commanded all to depart. BEDE. Josephus relates this was done in the ninth year of Claudius. Suetonius says that Claudius expelled the Jews from Rome.
18.3: 18.3 Tentmakers by trade. THE SAME. As exiles and strangers they build tents for themselves to use on the road, etc., down to and defends from the winds of ambushes by word and deed.
18.6: 18.6 Your blood. CHRYSOSTOM. He does this, so as not to terrify by word alone, and he discourses more vehemently, as one who had persuaded many.
18.7: 18.7 Titius Justus, one that worshiped God. Titius Justus was either the man's proper name, or he was so surnamed for the merit of his righteousness. This was not the Titus, disciple of Paul, to whom he wrote an Epistle and whom he ordained bishop of Crete; with whom Barnabas also, going up to Jerusalem, conferred the Gospel with the apostles, inquiring in their council whether he was rightly preaching that the Gentiles are saved through the baptism of faith without circumcision, not because he himself doubted this, but to confirm by the authority of the apostles the minds of those in doubt.
18.15: 18.15 But if they are questions about the word. Now evidently declared and narrated, that is the Gospel: and names (Jesus) and (of God) or (of God the Father). In the Greek: And all the Greeks seizing Sosthenes, etc.
18.18: 18.18 Who had shorn his head. RABANUS. Who had shorn his head is uncertain; yet it was Paul or Aquila; either from fear of the Jews, or from eagerness to convert them? It is said ambiguously, but according to Jerome it is to be understood of Paul.
18.22: 18.22 Caesarea. THE SAME. Caesarea is the metropolis of Cappadocia. For he had not yet come into Syrian Phoenicia.
18.27: 18.27 Helped much. Another translation: He profited much those who believed, through grace, which is what the Apostle writes: I planted, Apollos watered, 1 Corinthians 3, etc.
19.4: 19.4 John baptized. BEDE. John did not remit sins by his baptism, but taught repentance. For as circumcision in the patriarchs was the seal of the faith they had, so the penitent people received this washing as a seal of their devotion: which prefigured the baptism of Christ, in which remission takes place. RABANUS. That is not baptism which is not given in the name of the Trinity. Those baptized by Judas are not rebaptized, because in the faith of the Trinity; but those baptized by John are, because John baptizes in water only but Christ in the Holy Spirit. When therefore a good or bad minister baptizes, if the faith of the Trinity is full, the Lord baptizes; but those baptized with water only by John were baptized by Paul. BEDE. The question is, whether one who through ignorance was perhaps baptized by an unbaptized man, but of right faith, ought to be rebaptized? Which I think is expounded in this chapter. For what difference is it whether one were baptized then before the beginning of Christ's baptism, or now by someone without receiving the same? since those whom John baptized in faith and in the name of Christ to come he declared must be baptized again, saying: I baptize with water, he will baptize with the Holy Spirit.
19.7: 19.7 And all. RABANUS. The judgments of God are a great abyss. Behold Asia, unworthy of the visitation of the apostles, now consecrated by the apostolic number and lifted up by the gift of prophecy. And it is to be noted that the Holy Spirit showed signs of his coming here upon twelve disciples, and above upon a hundred and twenty (which number is completed by twelve taken ten times), that in Jerusalem, this in Ephesus, which is a city of the Greeks. In which it is shown that he fills with the Spirit only those (whether of the Jews or of the Gentiles) who are in Catholic unity.
19.9: 19.9 Disputing daily in the school. BEDE. From the fifth hour to the ninth and tenth: as is handed down by some: because he gave five hours to work, another five to teaching, two to food and prayer, which however is confirmed by no authority. In the school of Tyrannus. RABANUS. The name Tyrannus is put for dignity, or is a proper name, and is interpreted holding them, or confirming.
19.10: 19.10 For two years. At this time Paul in Ephesus wrote the first Epistle to the Corinthians.
19.12: 19.12 Handkerchiefs. RABANUS. Garments hanging from one side, or girdles or night garments, or a kind of sudarium, which the Hebrews use on the head.
19.13: 19.13 Exorcists. Solomon devised and taught his nation the ways of exorcism, that is of conjuration, by which unclean spirits driven out dared not return to men. This is done through reprobates for their own condemnation and the profit of those who see and hear: because although they despise those who work signs, yet they honor God, at whose invocation it is done.
19.14: 19.14 Seven sons, etc. BEDE. Since Satan transforms himself into an angel of light, etc., down to shows of which guards of the Church it is commanded: Catch us the little foxes that destroy the vineyards, Canticle 2.
19.19: 19.19 And many of them who had followed curious arts. BEDE. The industry of the magic art: whose followers deservedly burn their books, though valued at a great price, because they see the demons (whom they had served) call upon Jesus and honor his apostles.
19.21: 19.21 And when these things were ended, etc. CHRYSOSTOM. Having lived long enough in the city, etc., down to so everywhere he weaves in his works. To see Rome. RABANUS. He had perhaps not seen it before, or because he thought light the tribulation he was to suffer there; he says only to see, not to suffer much.
19.22: 19.22 Into Macedonia. RABANUS. He wished to pass from Asia, in which is Ephesus, into Europe, where Macedonia and Achaia are; and so to go again into Asia, that is to Jerusalem with the alms, about which he wrote to the Corinthians.
19.28: 19.28 Great is Diana of the Ephesians. BEDE. Diana, whom Demetrius said would perish, they on the contrary marvel at as great.
19.32: 19.32 Some therefore cried one thing, some another. That other thing which they cried was either that they should be dragged into the theater, or that some other god was great, or some other idol, or they were even casting reproaches at Paul.
19.34: 19.34 There was one voice of all, crying out for about two hours: Great is Diana of the Ephesians. Deservedly the Jews push the scribe Alexander forward out of that crowd which wholly worshiped Diana.
19.37: 19.37 Neither robbers of churches, nor blasphemers of your goddess. RABANUS. Sacrilegious are so called from profane diligence. For sacred signifies the clean and the profane.
19.40: 19.40 And when he had said this. He says this as a Jew, not wishing the Jews to be killed by the worshipers of idols; or he spoke as a Christian.
20.2: 20.2 Into Greece. Greece is the province of Achaia; Paul came to it after Macedonia: because he had so proposed, as was said above; he passes from Macedonia and Achaia to go to Jerusalem.
20.4: 20.4 Sopater. In the Hebrew Sopater is interpreted as the same as narrating the dispersion, or saving the dispersed.
20.7: 20.7 And on the first day of the week. It is called the name of a day, that it may be a preparation of virtue to be done and said. BEDE. The upper room, the height of the charisms. The night, the obscurity of the Scriptures, etc., down to he subjoined: These are the two Testaments.
20.9: 20.9 Eutychus, etc. THE SAME. In Hebrew he is interpreted senseless, in Greek fortunate, etc., down to that the memory of a teacher about to depart may be more closely fixed in the mind.
20.10: 20.10 When Paul went down, he fell on him. THE SAME. He went down and fell on him, embraced him, etc., down to and the sun of justice breathing upon him, he is brought back alive. For his soul is in him. RABANUS. That is, it had not wholly departed, or returned. He said this on account of the unbelievers, as: The girl is not dead, but sleeps: for thus despair is taken away.
20.16: 20.16 Pentecost. It is established that the time of Pascha and the times of Pentecost were celebrated in the days of the apostles.
20.31: 20.31 Remembering. RABANUS. What he had said to them, he wishes that to be kept in memory, for the memory of the divine precept is no small guard.
20.35: 20.35 It is more blessed. THE SAME. This is not read in the Gospel, for not all things have been written, but Paul perhaps heard this from the apostles, or received it from the Holy Spirit, or it can be said that, if not the words, Jesus indicated this sense, saying: Give to everyone who asks; and elsewhere: Do not take gold, etc. BEDE. He does not set rich almsgivers before those who, leaving all things, followed the Lord, but especially glorifies those who, renouncing all they possess, nonetheless labor working with their hands that they may have something to give to him who suffers need. You therefore bishops, be solicitous for the feeding of orphans, etc.
21.1: 21.1 And when, etc. To Cos, Rhodes, thence to Patara. RABANUS. Cos and Patara are islands.
21.8: 21.8 Of Philip the evangelist. For his ready office of preaching he deserved to be called evangelist.
21.9: 21.9 Now he had. RABANUS. Elsewhere the daughters of Philip the apostle are read to have been prophetesses, but the truth of this place is not to be contradicted, unless perhaps both are understood to have had prophetess daughters.
21.11: 21.11 Thus says the Holy Spirit. BEDE. He imitates the ancient prophets, who used to say: Thus says the Lord God, because the Holy Spirit, equally with the Father and the Son, is Lord and God, nor can the working be separated of those whose nature and will is one.
21.21: 21.21 Saying that they ought not. BEDE. As if they said: In the doctrine of Christ you condemn as sacrilegious, etc., down to but the Jews were not forbidden. Nor according. The Jews believing in Christ were not forbidden at that time to enter according to the law, the temple still standing and their religion, though they would have salvation in the sacraments of the New Testament, but believers from the Gentiles were forbidden to be converted to the law, who however were commanded to keep diligently the commandments of the law pertaining to morals and cleanness of body, such as: You shall not covet, etc. A fourfold synod was held at Jerusalem: the first was about the election of another apostle in place of Judas; the second about the election of the seven deacons; the third about circumcision not to be imposed on those who believed from the Gentiles; the fourth this, about the Jews at that time not being forbidden (where necessity required) to be initiated into legal ceremonies for the sake of the scandal of those who thought the apostles condemned the law of Moses as idolaters condemn doctrines.
21.24: 21.24 That the things which concerning you, etc. For you do not reprobate legal things as was said, but if he therefore celebrated, so that by a feigned action he might conceal his opinion, James would not say this.
21.27: 21.27 And when the seven days, etc. They were not yet completed, but their course was still going on, etc., down to lest the Romans come and take away the place and the nation.
21.35: 21.35 And when he came to the stairs. The stairs signify not of descent from the temple, but of ascent into the camp.
21.37: 21.37 Do you know Greek? RABANUS. It is a question or an affirmation, because (as is thought) the tribune spoke Greek, or, lest the Jews understand.
21.39: 21.39 From Tarsus, etc. THE SAME. Where he was taken with his parents and moved.
22.3: 22.3 Born in Tarsus. BEDE. Paul was born in the town of Galilee called Gischala, etc., down to so Christ, born in Bethlehem, was called a Nazarene. Zealous for the law. In the Greek: Zealous for the law of God existing, according to that: I bear them witness that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge, Romans 10.
22.7: 22.7 Saul, Saul. RABANUS. Some copies have: Saul, Saul, to show that Saul is named from the name of Saul.
22.9: 22.9 They heard. THE SAME. They understood, but only the sound of Paul's voice, or of him who spoke to Paul.
22.10: 22.10 And there. THE SAME. An example of humility, against disputing with teachers, and against presuming of ourselves as if taught by God.
22.13: 22.13 Brother Saul, look up. THE SAME. There were two things in Paul's eyes, blinding and enlightening: and therefore deservedly he believed.
22.14: 22.14 He has foreordained you. THE SAME. A fitting order: first, foreordained in the foreknowledge of God; then he knows the truth, sees the Just One, hears from his mouth; afterwards he becomes witness of what he knew, saw, heard.
22.17: 22.17 To be in a trance of mind. He does not tell this for elation, but out of necessity, that he may be seen fit to evangelize the Gentiles.
22.20: 22.20 I consented. By confessing that he consented, he notes that he did not kill, unless striking be taken for killing, or taking care to kill.
22.28: 22.28 I with a great sum. Another edition shows more plainly what the tribune said. The tribune said: Do you say so easily that you are a Roman citizen? for with how great a price did I obtain this citizenship. Citizenship. That is the social intercourse among citizens, or administration of the commonwealth. For the tribune could not fail to be a citizen of the Roman state, but he had bought fellowship in the city, to be a partaker. Paul was the more a Roman citizen in that he had it not by purchase but by birth.
23.3: 23.3 God shall strike you. RABANUS. He does not say, may God strike, because it is prophecy, not a curse, etc., down to but the Apostle spoke by divine inspiration.
23.5: 23.5 I knew not, brethren. That is I did not know he was Ananias; or he subtly says he does not know a prince, because the priesthood of the Jews is reprobated.
23.9: 23.9 What if a spirit? RABANUS. Here it appears, according to Jerome, that the Sadducees do not confess spirit and angels, and therefore the Pharisees name spirit and angel, because they knew this to be contrary to them.
23.10: 23.10 Lest Paul should be torn in pieces by them. THE SAME. The Sadducees wishing to seize him, or both contending at once.
23.12: 23.12 Bound themselves, saying. In Greek, anathematized: they know how great the authority of this word is who are alienated by priestly anathema from the fellowship of Christ and the Church.
23.23: 23.23 Prepare two hundred soldiers, etc. RABANUS. He bids this be done, lest the Jews carry him off, and the tribune himself be accused of a crime before the governor, as if about to receive money from the Jews, and the price of Paul's death.
24.14: 24.14 To my Father and God. RABANUS. Whose son I am shown to be, not servant, as is had in other codices.
24.21: 24.21 Except for this one. THE SAME. He says this by antiphrasis, for he knew this pleased them: as if he said I have committed nothing, except that I preached what they themselves believe.
24.23: 24.23 To minister to him of his own. THE SAME. To the disciples and companions; otherwise, he ordered that no one be forbidden to minister to him from his own goods or means.
24.25: 24.25 Trembling, etc., and hoping. THE SAME. Join thus: trembling and hoping, for these two he sent him away to free custody, for fear of God and hope of money.
24.27: 24.27 Left Paul bound. THE SAME. Whether Felix, living or dying, left Paul, is uncertain; but it seems better that, living, he granted a favor to the Jews.
25.1: 25.1 Festus therefore, when he was come into the province, etc. RABANUS. Understand the province of Palestine, as governors of Palestine, others always succeeding others, were sent by the Romans.
25.18: 25.18 Of whom, etc. THE SAME. For these causes, or things, or words: of whom I suspected, that is I expected from the accusers, or the evils of which I suspected; otherwise, of whom, that is of the accusers I suspected evil: because they brought no cause worthy of death.
25.19: 25.19 Their own superstition. RABANUS. He called the law of both, that is of Paul and of the Jews, superstition.
25.23: 25.23 With great pomp. THE SAME. That is with a great crowd surrounding them, or with great desire of hearing Paul. For pomp in the Greek is put phantasia, that is a manifold apparatus and show of royal office: with which she was thronged on every side.
26.8: 26.8 Why is it judged incredible? RABANUS. Or thus: King, what do you say? is it judged incredible with you? etc., by asking, as if he said: It is not incredible. He raised up the dead indeed before as an example of the future, or raises.
26.10: 26.10 When they were put to death I brought the sentence. THE SAME. Another edition: And I brought sentence that they be put to death, that is how they should be put to death I gave sentence. I brought sentence. I judged they should be put to death: he does not say I killed, unless perhaps what follows pertains to the killing: Punishing them, etc., and the more mad, etc.
26.14: 26.14 Against the goad. THE SAME. Hitherto you have resisted without a goad, but now if you resist you will kick against the goad, which is hard enough. The goad is correction itself. You are mad, Paul. BEDE. He thinks it madness that a bound man, having received a place for defending himself, etc., down to and the Prophet: He has not regarded vanities and false follies, Psalm 39.
26.24: 26.24 Many. RABANUS. The philosophers of the Gentiles changed their sects by much reading. To madness, understand of changeableness; or he calls madness the resurrection of the dead, which he announces.
27.1: 27.1 And when it was determined that he should sail, etc. In the Greek: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion.
27.2: 27.2 Adramyttium. RABANUS. That is sailing to Rome according to some, but better derived from the name of an African city which is called Adrumetum.
27.5: 27.5 We came to Lystra. BEDE. For Lystra, in the Greek Smyrna is written. Jerome, however, puts Myra.
27.9: 27.9 The fast. RABANUS. A great famine on the voyage making the sailors weaker. Others say it was then the Lent before the Lord's birth, which is not probable. It is better to think the fast of the seventh month, in which Gedaliah was killed. Or the day of the fast of the tenth month in January, when the captives in Babylon learned that the temple was destroyed.
27.12: 27.12 A harbor, etc. THE SAME. The harbor of Crete is that which is in Phoenix opposite Crete: they sought the harbor of Crete because they were sailing to Crete. Toward the southwest, etc. The southwest wind stands between the southern quarter and the western, inclining more to the west; the northwest between the northern and western, turned more to the west; and the province of Phoenix had Crete to the west.
27.13: 27.13 Assos. RABANUS. The name of a place so called, because from there ships loosed, going out to sea.
27.14: 27.14 Typhonic. Another translation: a stormy wind. Euroaquilo. RABANUS. That is Boreas, a wind between the north and the east; this wind was contrary to a ship about to sail to Phoenix.
27.17: 27.17 The Syrtis. THE SAME. Syrtis is said to be narrowness or tribulation.
27.21: 27.21 It was indeed necessary, etc. THE SAME. As if he said: You did not listen to God, because above Paul exhorted them; or I should have been listened to, that is that you should listen to me.
27.26: 27.26 But we must come to a certain island. THE SAME. As if he said: The prophecy about the island is a sign of truth, that when they come to it, they may be sure of their safety.
27.27: 27.27 In the Adriatic. A region to which they were sailing; or the name of a certain strait in the Tyrrhenian sea, or rather it seems the name of that land from which the Adriatic gulf is called. Otherwise, Adria is taken in the plural for rocks, and therefore the sailors thought a region appeared. In the Book of Hebrew names, Adria is said to be holding evils, or place of evils.
27.34: 27.34 To take food. BEDE. No one escapes the storms of the world except him who is fed with the bread of life, and who in the night of tribulations leans on wisdom, fortitude, temperance and justice, the help of the Lord shining forth obtains the harbor of salvation, so that, freed from the world, he seeks the flame of love by which the inner parts are warmed.
27.37: 27.37 We were in all souls. RABANUS. He does not say men, because perhaps there were also women; or, on account of the confusion of Christians, soldiers and sailors, it is so said.
27.41: 27.41 A place of two seas. BEDE. The Greeks call the sea Thalassa, etc., down to and the sea is called by the Greeks Thelasson.
28.2: 28.2 A fire. RABANUS. Some say pyra is the name of a wood.
28.8: 28.8 Dysentery or dysis. BEDE. It is a disease of the intestines. He healed him. Why does he heal by prayer an unbelieving sick man, who treats Timothy and Trophimus, sick believers, so as to cure one, leave the other? unless because he who was not living within was to be healed outwardly by a miracle: but this those did not need who lived wholesomely within.
28.13: 28.13 Puteoli. Puteoli is a place beyond Rome where Virgil made medicinal baths, each inscribed with its own title (as is said) against which sickness they availed. Hence the Salernitans, moved by envy, coming upon them with a strong hand, destroyed the titles and mutilated the buildings.
28.15: 28.15 The brethren, when they heard. RABANUS. Christians dwelling at Rome from where? it is clear that Paul did not first preach to the Romans.
28.30: 28.30 In a hired house. That is in free custody by which he was conducted, or in his own assembly in which he disputed against the Jews.
28.31: 28.31 Without prohibition. RABANUS. After the passion of the Lord in the twenty-fifth year, etc., down to Peter and Paul were crowned with martyrdom.
